intro.en: Dwell began as a verb of delay: Old English dwellan meant to lead astray or hold back. The idea of being held in one place softened into staying, then into living there, and finally into the mind staying on one thought.
intro.cn: dwell 起初是一个表示拖延的动词：古英语 dwellan 意为引入歧途或阻住。被阻在一处的想法软化为「停留」，再变成「住在那里」，最后变成心思停在一个念头上。

items.en: Old English dwellan means to lead astray or to delay.
items.cn: 古英语 dwellan 意为引入歧途或拖延。

items.en: Old Norse dvelja means to delay and also to stay in a place.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 dvelja 意为拖延，也指停留在某地。

items.en: Middle English dwellen shifts to tarrying and then to living somewhere.
items.cn: 中古英语 dwellen 转为停留，再转为居住。

items.en: The phrase dwell on appears for keeping the mind on one subject.
items.cn: 短语 dwell on 出现，指让心思停在一个题目上。

items.en: Engineers use dwell for the pause of a part within a cycle.
items.cn: 工程师用 dwell 指部件在一个循环中的停顿。

items.en: The verb is now literary for living, and common for brooding on a thought.
items.cn: 这个动词如今在「居住」义上偏书面，在「反复想」义上常用。

note.en: Dwell rhymes with swell and spell, while its neighbours name living somewhere formally and keeping the mind on a worry.
note.cn: dwell 与 swell、spell 押韵，而它的近义词则指正式地居住在某处，以及让心思停在一件忧心事上。

dict_mnemonic.text: dwell 的古英语 dwellan 本义是「引入歧途、拖住」——被拖住就是「停留」，停留久了就是「居住」。所以 dwell in the stone houses 是「住在石屋里」（偏书面），而 dwell on the past 是「心思停在过去出不来」，即「老想着、耿耿于怀」。名词 dwell 在机械里指「停留时间」，如活塞在上止点的短暂停顿。派生词 dweller 是「居民」，dwelling 是「住所」。过去式常用 dwelt。

root: 古英语 dwellan（引入歧途、拖住）→ 古诺斯语 dvelja（停留）→ 中古英语 dwellen（居住）→ dwell on（细想）

intro.en: Dumbfound is dumb joined to the tail of confound: dumb means unable to speak and confound means to pour together in confusion, so the compound is a surprise that empties both the mouth and the mind.

items.en: English confound is used for throwing something into confusion.

items.en: The compound dumbfound appears for making someone speechless with surprise.

intro.en: Dystrophy is dys- meaning bad plus trophe meaning nourishment, from Greek trephein to feed; the same trophe gives atrophy for no nourishment and hypertrophy for too much.
intro.cn: dystrophy 由 dys-（坏）加 trophe（营养）构成，trophe 源自希腊语 trephein「喂养」；同一个 trophe 给出 atrophy（无营养）与 hypertrophy（营养过度）。

items.en: The Greek prefix dys- means bad or difficult.
items.cn: 希腊语前缀 dys- 意为坏、困难。

items.en: Greek trephein means to nourish or to feed.
items.cn: 希腊语 trephein 意为滋养、喂养。

items.en: Greek trophe means nourishment, the root of the whole family.
items.cn: 希腊语 trophe 意为营养，是整个词族的词根。

items.en: Medicine coined dystrophy for tissue wasting from defective nourishment.

items.en: The inherited muscle disorders were grouped under the same name.

items.en: Dystrophin was named after the disease it fails to protect.

note.en: Dystrophy, atrophy and hypertrophy share the root trophe and differ only in the prefix: bad, without or over; the neighbours name wasting from other causes.
note.cn: dystrophy、atrophy 与 hypertrophy 共用词根 trophe，只差前缀：坏、无、过度；近义词则指称其他原因造成的萎缩。

dict_mnemonic.text: dystrophy ＝ dys-（坏）＋ troph-（营养，希腊语 trophe，源自 trephein 喂养）＋ -y（状态）＝「营养坏了的状态」。同根三兄弟只差前缀：a-（无）→ atrophy 萎缩（不用就退化）；hyper-（过度）→ hypertrophy 肥大（练过头就变大）；dys-（坏）→ dystrophy 营养障碍（供养本身出了问题）。最常见的是 muscular dystrophy 肌营养不良，其中 Duchenne 型因缺少 dystrophin（抗肌萎缩蛋白）而发病，蛋白名正是从病名来的。此外还有 corneal dystrophy 角膜营养不良、retinal dystrophy 视网膜营养不良。注意与 malnutrition 区分：后者是吃不够，前者是组织自身利用不了营养。

senses.title: Evaporating quickly
senses.definition: of a liquid or substance, turning into vapour rapidly at ordinary temperatures
senses.definitionCN: 指液体或物质在常温下迅速变成蒸气
senses.example: The solvent is volatile and must be handled inside the fume hood.
senses.exampleCN: 这种溶剂易挥发，必须在通风柜内操作。
senses.why: The Latin adjective meant flying; a liquid that flies off into the air keeps the literal image.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁形容词意为「会飞的」；飞进空气里的液体保留了字面意象。

senses.title: Moving unpredictably in price
senses.definition: of a market or price, rising and falling sharply without a stable trend
senses.definitionCN: 指市场或价格大起大落，没有稳定趋势
senses.example: Oil prices stayed volatile through the whole quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 整个季度油价都在剧烈波动。
senses.why: Finance borrowed the flying image: numbers that will not settle are numbers that keep taking off.
senses.whyCN: 金融借用了「飞」的意象：不肯落地的数字，就是不断起飞。

senses.title: Likely to change suddenly
senses.definition: of a situation or condition, liable to change quickly and dangerously
senses.definitionCN: 指局势或状况可能迅速而危险地变化
senses.example: The region's politics remain volatile after the election.
senses.exampleCN: 选举之后，该地区的政治局势仍不稳定。
senses.why: The flying image applies to a whole order, not just a price: what will not stay put can also break apart.
senses.whyCN: 「飞」的意象适用于整个秩序，而非单一价格：不肯停在原位的，也可能四分五裂。

senses.title: Quick to anger
senses.definition: of a person or temper, becoming angry suddenly and without much warning
senses.definitionCN: 指人或脾气突然发火，且少有预警
senses.example: His volatile temper made the meeting difficult.
senses.exampleCN: 他暴躁的脾气让会议很难进行。
senses.why: A temper is weather inside a person, and the same refusal to settle now describes a mood.
senses.whyCN: 脾气是一个人内心的天气，同一种「不肯安定」如今用来描述情绪。

senses.title: Lasting only a short time
senses.definition: of fame, memory or a condition, passing away quickly
senses.definitionCN: 指名声、记忆或状态很快消逝
senses.example: The band enjoyed volatile fame in the early years.
senses.exampleCN: 这支乐队早年的名声来得快去得也快。
senses.why: Fame flies past, so the literal flight becomes a statement about how long something lasts.
senses.whyCN: 名声会飞逝，于是字面的「飞行」变成对事物持续多久的陈述。

senses.title: Dangerously reactive
senses.definition: of a substance or mixture, able to react, ignite or explode easily
senses.definitionCN: 指物质或混合物容易反应、着火或爆炸
senses.example: The warehouse stored volatile chemicals away from any flame.
senses.exampleCN: 仓库把易反应的化学品存放在远离火源的地方。
senses.why: Reactive substances take off as heat and gas, which is the flying image made dangerous.
senses.whyCN: 反应性物质会以热与气体的形式腾起，这就是「飞」的意象变得危险。

senses.title: Wavering in data or results
senses.definition: of measurements or performance, varying widely from one reading to the next
senses.definitionCN: 指测量值或表现各次之间差异很大
senses.example: The sensor gave volatile readings during the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴期间传感器读数起伏不定。
senses.why: A reading that jumps like a flying thing cannot be trusted as a measurement.
senses.whyCN: 像飞物一样跳动的读数，无法作为可靠的测量值。

senses.title: Not durable in alliance
senses.definition: of a partnership or agreement, likely to break or shift soon
senses.definitionCN: 指伙伴关系或协议可能很快破裂或改变
senses.example: The two parties formed a volatile alliance that lasted one season.
senses.exampleCN: 两方结成了一个只维持一季的脆弱联盟。
senses.why: An alliance that keeps shifting has no stable ground to stand on.
senses.whyCN: 不断变动的联盟，没有稳定地面可以站立。

senses.title: Lost when power is cut
senses.definition: of computer memory, holding data only while power is supplied
senses.definitionCN: 指计算机存储器只在供电时保存数据
senses.example: The device keeps the log in volatile memory until it is saved.
senses.exampleCN: 该设备把日志保存在易失性存储器中，直到被写入。
senses.why: Memory contents fly away when the power stops, so the technical name keeps the literal flight.
senses.whyCN: 断电时存储内容会飞走，因此这个技术名称保留了字面的「飞行」。

intro.en: Volatile comes from a Latin adjective for flying: the same word covers vapour that flies off, prices that will not settle, a temper that flares and memory that vanishes.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语表示「会飞的」形容词：同一个词覆盖飞走的蒸气、不肯落定的价格、突然爆发的脾气，以及会消失的记忆。

items.en: volare meant to fly, to move through the air.
items.cn: volare 意为「飞、在空中移动」。

items.en: volatilis described what flies or passes quickly, including birds and fleeting things.
items.cn: volatilis 描述会飞或迅速消逝的东西，包括鸟与短暂之物。

items.en: English adopted the adjective in the sixteenth century with the sense of flying or fleeting; the exact first date is approximate but the root is clear.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入这个形容词，意为「飞行的、短暂的」；具体首见年份为约数，但词根清楚。

items.en: Chemistry made the flying literal: a volatile liquid is one that takes off as vapour.
items.cn: 化学让「飞」变得字面化：挥发性液体就是会以蒸气形式飞走的液体。

items.en: Finance and politics extended the image to prices and situations that will not stay put.
items.cn: 金融与政治把这个意象扩展到不肯停在原位的价格与局势。

items.en: Computing named memory volatile because its contents fly away when the power stops.
items.cn: 计算机领域把存储器称为易失的，因为断电时其内容会飞走。

note.en: The first group shares the flying root or looks close; the second group names nearby kinds of instability, and the note separates them from mere energy.
note.cn: 第一组共享「飞」的词根或形音相近；第二组是邻近的不稳定类说法，说明中把它们与单纯的「精力旺盛」分开。

entries.definition: The noun for the tendency to evaporate or to change sharply.
entries.definitionCN: 指易挥发或剧烈变化的性质。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to make a substance evaporate or to become vapour.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，指使物质挥发或变成蒸气。

entries.definition: Not evaporating easily, or, in computing, keeping data when power is off.
entries.definitionCN: 指不易挥发，或在计算机中断电仍保存数据。

entries.definition: Able to turn to many uses; it looks close but its root is turning, not flying.
entries.definitionCN: 指能转向多种用途；形近，但词根是「转动」，不是「飞」。

entries.definition: Likely to change, fall or fail; broader and plainer than volatile.
entries.definitionCN: 指可能变化、倒下或失败；比本词更宽泛、更朴素。

entries.definition: Impossible to forecast; it stresses the lack of warning rather than the size of the swing.
entries.definitionCN: 指无法预测；强调缺乏预警，而非波动幅度。

entries.definition: Able to blow up, or a temper that erupts violently; it stresses the burst itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指会爆炸，或脾气猛烈爆发；强调爆发本身。

entries.definition: Full of energy and force; it describes strength in action, not instability or evaporation.
entries.definitionCN: 指精力充沛、有力；描述行动中的力量，而非不稳定或挥发。

entries.definition: Passing quickly; it covers the short-lived sense without the chemistry or finance ones.
entries.definitionCN: 指迅速消逝；只覆盖「短暂」这一义，不含化学与金融义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin flying root, the real chemistry and finance phrases, and the real contrast with vigorous.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁「飞」词根、真实的化学与金融搭配，以及与 vigorous 的真实区别。

normal.en: The root means fly: a volatile liquid flies into the air, and volatile prices fly up and down.
normal.cn: 词根意为「飞」：易挥发的液体飞进空气，易波动的价格上下飞。

normal.en: Volatile compound, volatile market and volatile memory are three real phrases from three fields.
normal.cn: 挥发性化合物、动荡的市场与易失性存储器是来自三个领域的真实搭配。

normal.en: The same word covers a solvent, a temper and a share price because all refuse to stay put.
normal.cn: 同一个词覆盖溶剂、脾气与股价，因为它们都不肯停在原地。

normal.en: Volatility is the noun; volatilize is the verb that sends a substance into vapour.
normal.cn: volatility 是名词；volatilize 是把物质送进蒸气的动词。

normal.en: Versatile is about turning, volatile is about flying; one changes uses, the other changes state.
normal.cn: versatile 说的是「转」，volatile 说的是「飞」；一个换用途，一个换状态。

abstract.en: What flies cannot be held; volatility is a warning that the present reading is not a promise.
abstract.cn: 会飞的东西握不住；波动性是一个警告：此刻的读数不是承诺。

abstract.en: A volatile temper and a volatile market share one structure: energy with no container.
abstract.cn: 暴躁的脾气与动荡的市场共享一个结构：没有容器的能量。

abstract.en: The word describes disappearance as well as change, which is why memory and fame are called volatile.
abstract.cn: 这个词既描述变化，也描述消失，所以记忆与名声也被称为短暂易逝。

examples.en: The lab stores volatile solvents in a cool cabinet away from heat.
examples.cn: 实验室把易挥发溶剂存放在远离热源的阴凉柜里。

examples.en: Currency markets grew volatile after the announcement.
examples.cn: 公告发布后，货币市场变得动荡。

examples.en: The old photographs are fading because the dyes are volatile.
examples.cn: 这些老照片正在褪色，因为染料不稳定。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「佛勒泰尔」——拉丁语「会飞的」：说走就走

root: 来自拉丁语 volatilis「会飞的、短暂的」← volare「飞」，经法语进入英语，十六世纪起用；化学义让「飞」字面化，金融与计算义再作延伸。词根清楚，首见年份为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses run from an evaporating liquid through prices, politics, temper, fame, reactive chemicals, readings, alliances and computer memory.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从挥发的液体，经过价格、政治、脾气、名声、反应性化学品、读数、联盟，最后到计算机存储器。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: liquid in an open beaker keeps disappearing upward while a price curve jumps on the screen.
core.cn: 核心意象：敞口烧杯里的液体不断向上消失，屏幕上的价格曲线同时剧烈跳动。

branches.en: THE SUBSTANCE: a liquid that evaporates or a chemical that reacts dangerously.
branches.cn: 物质：会蒸发的液体，或会危险反应的化学品。

branches.en: THE NUMBERS: prices and readings that will not settle.
branches.cn: 数字：不肯落定的价格与读数。

branches.en: THE SITUATION: a political order or alliance likely to break.
branches.cn: 局势：可能破裂的政治秩序或联盟。

branches.en: THE TEMPER: anger that flares without warning.
branches.cn: 脾气：无预警爆发的怒火。

branches.en: THE VANISHING: fame and memory that pass, and data lost with the power.
branches.cn: 消失：消逝的名声与记忆，以及随断电丢失的数据。

intro.en: Volatile is a Latin flying stem with an adjective ending; chemistry, finance and computing keep adding noun and verb forms around it.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁「飞」词干加形容词词尾；化学、金融与计算不断在它周围添名词与动词形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies volare, volatilis and volatilitas; English builds volatility, volatilize and nonvolatile on the same stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了 volare、volatilis 与 volatilitas；英语在同一词干上构成 volatility、volatilize 与 nonvolatile。

items.example: The root supplies the flight.
items.exampleCN: 词根提供飞行。

items.example: The adjective adds the quality.
items.exampleCN: 形容词加上性质。

items.example: It marks the tendency.
items.exampleCN: 它标记倾向。

items.example: The borrowed word keeps the flight.
items.exampleCN: 借入的词保留飞行。

items.example: The Latin noun names the quality.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁名词命名这种性质。

items.example: It forms volatility.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 volatility。

items.example: It forms volatilize, to send into vapour.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 volatilize，即使之挥发。

items.example: It forms volatilization.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 volatilization。

items.example: It forms nonvolatile, the settled case.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 nonvolatile，即安定的情形。

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加性质名词词尾构成，义为「挥发性；波动性」
由形容词加使动词尾构成，义为「使挥发」
由挥发动词加动作名词词尾构成，义为「挥发过程」
由否定前缀加本词构成，义为「不挥发的」

definition_zh: 适应度；健康；体能；适合
definition_en: the state of being physically healthy, the quality of being suitable, or in biology the relative reproductive success of a variant
core_image: 一只体态匀称的鹿站在坡上，旁边画着后代数量刻度与心率曲线，背景有哑铃剪影
scene: 同一片草场上有三只同种甲虫，各自留下的后代数量差了三倍。 Reproductive fitness is measured not by how long an insect lives but by how many of its young survive.
sceneCN: 这里 fitness 指「（生殖）适应度」（第 3 个义项：个体在下一代基因库中所占的相对贡献）；句意：生殖适应度不看昆虫活多久，而看它有多少后代存活。图中可辨识物件：同种甲虫、后代数量刻度、存活率曲线、草场样方。

pos.zh: 健康；体能；适合；适应度（多为不可数）

derivatives.zh: 健康的；合适的 / 适合；安装

senses.title: Physical condition
senses.definition: the condition of being physically healthy and strong
senses.definitionCN: 身体健康、有力的状态
senses.example: Regular hill walking improved his fitness within a season.
senses.exampleCN: 经常走山路使他的体能在一个季节内提高。
senses.why: fit first meant 'suited, well matched', and a body suited to its tasks came to be called fit.
senses.whyCN: fit 最初意为「合适的、匹配良好的」，适合其任务的身体便被称为 fit。

senses.title: Suitability or match
senses.definition: the quality of being suitable for a purpose or a position
senses.definitionCN: 适合某用途或某职位的性质
senses.example: The fitness of the site for a wetland was assessed first.
senses.exampleCN: 首先评估了该地块作为湿地的适合性。
senses.why: this is the oldest branch: a thing fits a slot, and its fittingness is its fitness.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一支：一物契合一个位置，其契合程度就是它的适合性。

senses.title: Evolutionary fitness
senses.titleCN: 进化适应度：后代的相对贡献
senses.definition: in biology, an individual's relative contribution of offspring to the next generation
senses.definitionCN: 生物学中个体对下一代基因库的相对后代贡献
senses.example: Fitness is measured relative to other individuals, not on an absolute scale.
senses.exampleCN: 适应度是相对于其他个体测量的，而非绝对尺度。
senses.why: biology took the 'goodness of fit' idea and made it about fit between organism and environment, expressed as offspring.
senses.whyCN: 生物学借用了「契合度」的概念，把它用于生物与环境之间的匹配，并以后代数量表达。

senses.title: Inclusive fitness
senses.titleCN: 广义适合度：含亲属的后代
senses.definition: the fitness gained through one's own offspring plus the offspring helped in relatives
senses.definitionCN: 由自身后代加上帮助亲属所增后代构成的适合度
senses.example: Helpers at the nest raise the inclusive fitness of their siblings.
senses.exampleCN: 巢边的帮手提高了其手足的广义适合度。
senses.why: once shared genes matter, helping a relative counts as part of one's own reproductive score.
senses.whyCN: 一旦共享基因被计入，帮助亲属也算进自身的繁殖得分。

senses.title: Fitness landscape
senses.titleCN: 适应度地形：把适合度画成山丘
senses.definition: a model that maps genotypes or traits onto reproductive success as a surface
senses.definitionCN: 把基因型或性状映射为繁殖成功的曲面模型
senses.example: The population climbed a local peak on the fitness landscape.
senses.exampleCN: 该群体在适应度地形上爬上一座局部山峰。
senses.why: the abstract score becomes a shape that can be walked, so peaks and valleys stand for good and poor combinations.
senses.whyCN: 抽象分数变成一个可行走的形状，峰与谷代表好与差的组合。

senses.title: Fitness testing and training
senses.titleCN: 体测与健身：日常健康语境
senses.definition: the everyday use for measured physical capacity and for gym training
senses.definitionCN: 日常语境中指可测量的身体能力与健身训练
senses.example: The team ran a fitness test before the season began.
senses.exampleCN: 赛季开始前球队做了体能测试。
senses.why: sport fixed the word to measurable capacity such as endurance and strength.
senses.whyCN: 体育把这个词固定到可测量的能力上，如耐力与力量。

senses.title: Statistical goodness of fit
senses.titleCN: 统计拟合优度：模型与数据的贴合
senses.definition: in statistics, how well a model or curve matches observed data
senses.definitionCN: 统计学中模型或曲线与观测数据的贴合程度
senses.example: The fitness of the model was poor at high temperatures.
senses.exampleCN: 这个模型在高温下的拟合优度很差。
senses.why: the same 'fit' is used for a curve fitting points, with no biological content at all.
senses.whyCN: 同一个 fit 也用于曲线贴合数据点，完全不含生物学内容。

senses.title: Suitability for a post or role
senses.definition: the quality of being qualified for a role or office
senses.definitionCN: 胜任某角色或职位的资格
senses.example: The committee questioned his fitness for the chair.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会质疑他是否适合担任主席。
senses.why: institutional life keeps the oldest sense alive: fitness is fitness for something named.
senses.whyCN: 制度生活保留了最古老的义项：适合性总是对某个被命名的东西而言。

intro.en: Fitness is fit plus -ness. The adjective fit has an uncertain origin, and the biological sense was fixed in the nineteenth century. Dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: fitness 由 fit 加 -ness 构成。形容词 fit 的来源不确定，生物学义在 19 世纪固定下来。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Fit appears in the thirteenth to fourteenth centuries meaning 'suitable, well matched'; its earlier origin is uncertain, and no source is agreed.
items.cn: fit 于 13 至 14 世纪出现，意为「合适的、匹配良好的」；其更早来源不确定，学界没有一致结论。

items.en: A separate noun fit meant a bout or a song, and some dictionaries suspect a link with the adjective; this remains a hypothesis, not a demonstrated source.
items.cn: 另有一个名词 fit 指一阵发作或一首歌，部分词典怀疑它与形容词有关；这仍属假说，而非已证实的来源。

items.en: Fitness is recorded in the sixteenth century as 'suitableness', before any health sense.
items.cn: fitness 于 16 世纪有记录，意为「合适」，早于任何健康义。

items.en: The 'physical condition' sense grows in the nineteenth century with organised sport and gymnasium culture.
items.cn: 「体能」义随 19 世纪有组织的体育与健身房文化而发展。

items.en: Darwin and Spencer made fitness a technical measure of reproductive success, later formalised as relative genetic contribution.
items.cn: 达尔文与斯宾塞把 fitness 变成繁殖成功的术语指标，后来形式化为相对基因贡献。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-English origin of fit is unknown, and any reconstructed form offered for it is speculative.
items.cn: 来源不确定：fit 在英语之前的来源不明，凡为它给出的重构形式均属推测。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes from the fit family and its homographs; group two holds measures and near terms from biology and sport.
note.cn: 第一组是 fit 词族及同形词的形近词；第二组是生物学与体育中的指标与近义词。

entries.definition: Healthy, suitable, or to make something match. Fitness is the noun of state built on it.
entries.definitionCN: 指健康的、合适的，或使某物相配；fitness 是由它构成的状态名词。

entries.definition: Either 'suitable' or the act of trying on clothes. It is not the biological measure.
entries.definitionCN: 或指「恰当的」，或指试衣；它不是生物学指标。

entries.definition: Not healthy or not suitable, the direct negation of fit.
entries.definitionCN: 指不健康或不合适，是 fit 的直接否定。

entries.definition: An old spelling of fitness found in sixteenth-century texts; it is the same word, not a variant sense.
entries.definitionCN: 16 世纪文本中的旧拼法；是同一个词，并非另一义项。

entries.definition: The same biological measure spelled out: relative contribution of offspring. It avoids confusion with gym fitness.
entries.definitionCN: 同一生物学指标的完整说法：后代的相对贡献；可避免与健身义混淆。

entries.definition: General physical and mental well-being. It is not a relative measure and carries no genetic meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 指总体的身心安好；不是相对指标，也不含遗传含义。

entries.definition: The state of a body or machine, often used in sport for endurance. It is broader than fitness and less measured.
entries.definitionCN: 指身体或机器的状态，体育中常指耐力；比 fitness 更宽泛、更少量化。

entries.definition: A fitted trait. Fitness is the reproductive score that such traits tend to raise.
entries.definitionCN: 指适应出来的性状；fitness 是这类性状往往会提高的繁殖得分。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: fit 'suited' + -ness 'state': the state of being well matched.
normal.cn: fit「合适的」+ -ness「状态」：匹配良好的状态。

normal.en: The family runs fit, fitness, fitting, unfit, fitly.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 fit、fitness、fitting、unfit、fitly。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: physical fitness, fitness test, reproductive fitness, fitness landscape.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出义项：体能、体能测试、生殖适应度、适应度地形。

normal.en: In biology, always ask what fitness is relative to; it has no absolute zero.
normal.cn: 在生物学中，总要问适应度是相对于谁；它没有绝对零点。

normal.en: Do not read reproductive fitness as physical health; the two senses are far apart.
normal.cn: 不要把生殖适应度读成身体健康；这两个义项相距很远。

abstract.en: Picture a key that turns smoothly in one lock and jams in another.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙在一把锁里顺滑转动，在另一把里卡住。

abstract.en: Picture a scoreboard that counts surviving young instead of years lived.
abstract.cn: 想象一块记分牌数的是存活后代而不是寿命。

abstract.en: Picture a hill map where each step uphill means more offspring.
abstract.cn: 想象一张山丘地图，每向上一步就意味着更多后代。

examples.en: Fitness in evolutionary biology is always relative to the rest of the population.
examples.cn: 进化生物学中的适应度总是相对于群体其余个体而言。

examples.en: Her fitness improved after three months of swimming.
examples.cn: 游了三个月后，她的体能提高了。

examples.en: The model's fitness to the data was tested at five sites.
examples.cn: 这个模型对数据的拟合优度在五个地点接受了检验。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「肥（fit）得合适」——身子合适叫健康，基因合适叫适应度 → 体能、适合、适应度

root: 英语 fit「合适的」+ -ness；fit 的英语之前来源不确定（相关假说均未证实）；生物学义由达尔文与斯宾塞在 19 世纪固定为繁殖成功的相对指标。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one idea: being well matched, whether a body to its tasks, a word to a post, an organism to its habitat, a relative's genes to yours, a model to data, or a curve to points.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个观念展开：匹配良好——身体与任务、人与职位、生物与生境、亲属基因与你、模型与数据、曲线与数据点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body that fits its work, with offspring counted beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一副与工作相合的身体，旁边记着后代数量。

branches.en: BODY: health and measured capacity are the everyday face of being fit.
branches.cn: 身体：健康与可测能力是「合适」的日常面孔。

branches.en: SUITABILITY: the oldest sense, fitness for a purpose, a site or a post.
branches.cn: 适合性：最古老的义项，对用途、地块或职位的适合。

branches.en: REPRODUCTION: fitness becomes a relative count of descendants, own and shared.
branches.cn: 繁殖：适应度变成后代数量的相对计数，含自身与共享部分。

branches.en: MODEL: the score is drawn as a landscape of peaks and valleys.
branches.cn: 模型：得分被画成峰谷起伏的地形。

branches.en: STATISTICS: the same word measures how well a curve fits data.
branches.cn: 统计：同一个词衡量曲线与数据的贴合程度。

intro.en: Fitness is a short English adjective plus the native noun suffix -ness; it has no Latin affix structure of its own.
intro.cn: fitness 是简短英语形容词加本族名词后缀 -ness；它本身没有拉丁词缀结构。

latinIntro.en: The word has no Latin family; its relatives are English formations such as fitting, unfit and fitly.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词族；其同族词是 fitting、unfit、fitly 等英语构词。

items.example: Fitness varies with the environment.
items.exampleCN: 适应度随环境而变。

items.example: The seed is fit for dispersal by wind.
items.exampleCN: 这粒种子适合随风传播。

items.example: A fitting end to the dry season was a gentle rain.
items.exampleCN: 旱季的一个恰当收尾是一场细雨。

items.example: The wet field was unfit for grazing.
items.exampleCN: 湿透的田地不适合放牧。

items.example: The hut was fitly placed above the flood line.
items.exampleCN: 小屋恰当地建在洪水线之上。

items.example: The lighter seeds are fitter for wind travel.
items.exampleCN: 更轻的种子更适合随风传播。

items.example: The boat was refitted for the survey.
items.exampleCN: 这条船为调查重新装配。

items.example: The field outfit included nets and jars.
items.exampleCN: 野外装备包括网与罐。

definition_zh: 统计上；从统计角度看；在统计意义下
definition_en: in terms of statistics, or by the methods and standards of statistical analysis
core_image: 两支几乎重合的曲线落在同一条误差带里，标尺显示两者的差距不足以判定不同
scene: 这里指「统计上」。 Statistically, the two treatments performed the same.
sceneCN: 这里 statistically 是「从统计角度看」（第 1 个义项：依据统计方法判断，而非凭印象）；句意：从统计上看，两种疗法的效果相同。图中可辨识物件：误差带、重叠区间、标尺、两条几乎重合的曲线。

pos.zh: 统计上；从统计角度看；在统计意义下

collocations.zh: 在统计上具有代表性的

senses.title: By statistical methods
senses.definition: in a way that uses statistical methods or rests on summarized numerical evidence
senses.definitionCN: 以使用统计方法或依据汇总数值证据的方式
senses.example: Statistically, the survey is the best evidence we have.
senses.exampleCN: 从统计上看，这次调查是我们手上最好的证据。
senses.why: The adverb -ly turns the adjective into a standpoint: the speaker asks the listener to judge the claim by counting and probability rather than by impression.
senses.whyCN: 副词词尾 -ly 把形容词变成一种立场：说话人要求听者用计数与概率而不是凭印象来判断这一说法。

senses.title: At the threshold of significance
senses.titleCN: 达到统计显著：差距大到不像偶然
senses.definition: used with significant, meaning that the observed difference is large enough relative to random variation to be unlikely by chance
senses.definitionCN: 与 significant 连用，表示观察到的差异相对于随机波动足够大，不太可能出于偶然
senses.example: The new drug lowered blood pressure statistically significantly.
senses.exampleCN: 新药在统计上显著降低了血压。
senses.why: This is the most common use in research writing: the adverb tells the reader that the result passed a pre-set probability test, not that the effect was large in daily life.
senses.whyCN: 这是研究写作中最常见的用法：副词告诉读者结果通过了预设的概率检验，并不表示效果在日常生活中很大。

senses.title: In terms of calculated probability
senses.definition: used to state how likely something is according to probability calculated from data
senses.definitionCN: 用于说明依据数据计算出的概率，某事有多大的可能性
senses.example: Statistically, a passenger is safer in a bus than in a car.
senses.exampleCN: 从统计概率看，乘客坐公交车比坐小汽车更安全。
senses.why: Here the adverb shifts the frame from one journey to many journeys, so that risk is read off a distribution rather than off a single event.
senses.whyCN: 这里副词把视角从一次行程移到许多次行程，于是风险是从分布上读出的，而不是从单一事件读出的。

senses.title: With no detectable difference
senses.definition: used with words such as indistinguishable or equivalent, meaning that the data show no difference large enough to detect
senses.definitionCN: 与 indistinguishable、equivalent 等词连用，表示数据显示不出足够大的差异
senses.example: The two samples were statistically indistinguishable.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个样本在统计上无法区分。
senses.why: Statistically here marks a limit of evidence, not a proof of sameness: the method cannot separate the cases, which is a different claim from saying they are identical.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 statistically 标记证据的极限，而不是证明相同：方法无法把两者分开，这与「它们完全相同」是不同的主张。

senses.title: As a representative sample
senses.definition: used of a sample, meaning that its composition matches the larger population closely enough for inference
senses.definitionCN: 用于样本，表示其构成与更大总体足够接近，可以进行推断
senses.example: The panel was statistically representative of the electorate.
senses.exampleCN: 这个小组在统计上代表了全体选民。
senses.why: Representativeness is a statistical property, not a moral one; the adverb says the sample was checked against known proportions of the population.
senses.whyCN: 代表性是一种统计属性，而不是道德属性；副词说明该样本已对照总体的已知比例作过检验。

senses.title: As a way of framing a claim
senses.titleCN: 从统计角度来说（话语标记）
senses.definition: used as a discourse marker to announce that the following statement is a statistical generalization rather than a personal observation
senses.definitionCN: 作话语标记，提示接下来的陈述是统计概括，而不是个人观察
senses.example: Statistically speaking, most errors happen in the first week.
senses.exampleCN: 从统计角度来说，大多数错误发生在第一周。
senses.why: The phrase softens and frames: it warns the listener that exceptions exist, while asserting that the pattern holds across the counted cases.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语起缓冲与框定作用：它提醒听者存在例外，同时断言这一模式在被计数的案例中成立。

senses.title: On average, in the typical case
senses.titleCN: 按平均值、在典型情况下
senses.definition: in the average case, as opposed to an extreme or atypical one
senses.definitionCN: 在平均值情形下，而不是在极端或非典型情形下
senses.example: Statistically, the average household spends a fifth of its income on housing.
senses.exampleCN: 从统计平均看，普通家庭把五分之一的收入花在住房上。
senses.why: Averages hide variation, and the adverb signals that the statement is about the middle of a distribution, where no single family need actually sit.
senses.whyCN: 平均值会掩盖差异，这个副词提示该陈述针对分布的中间位置，而未必有任何一个家庭真的处在那里。

senses.title: Too small to matter in practice
senses.titleCN: 统计上可忽略：效应小到无实际意义
senses.definition: used of an effect or risk, meaning that it is measurably present but so small that it can be disregarded in practice
senses.definitionCN: 用于效应或风险，表示它在测量上确实存在，但小到在实际中可忽略
senses.example: The added risk was statistically negligible.
senses.exampleCN: 增加的风险在统计上可忽略不计。
senses.why: This sense separates statistical existence from practical importance: a difference can be real in the data and still be too small to act on.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项把「统计上存在」与「实际重要」分开：差异在数据中可能真实存在，却仍小到不值得采取行动。

intro.en: Statistically is statistical plus the native adverb ending -ly, whose Old English ancestor -lice marked manner. Statistical itself rests on statistics, a German academic coinage from New Latin statisticum and Latin status.
intro.cn: statistically 是 statistical 加本族副词词尾 -ly，其古英语前身 -lice 标记方式。statistical 又建立在 statistics 之上，后者是德国学界由新拉丁 statisticum 与拉丁 status 构成的造词。

items.en: Latin status 'condition, state' comes from stare 'to stand' and gives the whole family its base.
items.cn: 拉丁 status「状况、国家」出自 stare「站立」，为整个词族提供词基。

items.en: Statistik was fixed in 1749 as the name of the descriptive science of state facts; English statistics followed late in the century.
items.cn: Statistik 在 1749 年被固定为描述国家事实的学问之名；英语 statistics 在该世纪后期跟进。

items.en: The adjective statistical was formed on statistics and later applied to probability and sampling.
items.cn: 形容词 statistical 由 statistics 构成，后来应用于概率与抽样。

items.en: The Old English suffix -lice, later -ly, formed manner adverbs from adjectives; English applied it freely to statistical once the adjective existed.
items.cn: 古英语后缀 -lice（后为 -ly）由形容词构成方式副词；statistical 一旦存在，英语便自由地加上这一词尾。

items.en: In the twentieth century statistically fixed its collocations in research writing, above all statistically significant, and later statistically indistinguishable and statistically negligible.
items.cn: 二十世纪，statistically 在研究写作中固定了搭配，最重要的是 statistically significant，后来又出现 statistically indistinguishable 与 statistically negligible。

items.en: The exact first English citation of statistically is uncertain. The deeper root of stare is reconstructed as Indo-European *sta-, a reconstruction rather than a recorded form.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：statistically 的英语最早书证年代不确定。stare 的更深词根被重构为印欧语 *sta-，属重构形式，并非有记录的真实词形。

note.en: The first group separates the statistics family by part of speech; the second gives near-synonyms for the standpoint the adverb marks.
note.cn: 第一组按词性区分 statistics 词族；第二组给出与该副词所标立场相近的说法。

entries.definition: Describes a noun, such as a method or a result. Statistically describes how a verb is done or how a claim is framed.
entries.definitionCN: 修饰名词，如方法或结果；statistically 描述动作怎样完成或主张如何被框定。

entries.definition: The field or the data. It cannot stand where the adverb stands.
entries.definitionCN: 指学科或数据，不能出现在副词的位置上。

entries.definition: One computed number. The adverb never names a number; it names a way of judging.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个计算出的数值；副词从不命名数字，而是命名判断方式。

entries.definition: The analyst. Statistically refers to the method the analyst uses, not the analyst.
entries.definitionCN: 指分析者；statistically 指分析者所用的方法，而不是分析者本人。

entries.definition: Expressed as figures. It does not say whether the figures were sampled or tested.
entries.definitionCN: 指以数字表达，并不说明这些数字是否经过抽样或检验。

entries.definition: In terms of quantity rather than quality. It is broader and less technical than statistically.
entries.definitionCN: 指从数量而非性质角度，比 statistically 更宽泛、更不技术化。

entries.definition: In terms of probability. A model can be probabilistic without using measured data, so the words are not interchangeable.
entries.definitionCN: 指从概率角度；模型可以是概率性的而不使用实测数据，因此两者不能随意互换。

entries.definition: The everyday phrase for the middle of a distribution; it matches the 'typical case' sense but not the significance sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指分布中间的日常说法；它对应「典型情况」义项，但不对应显著性义项。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: statistical + -ly: judge the claim by the numbers.
normal.cn: statistical + -ly：用数字来判断这一说法。

normal.en: The family runs statistics, statistic, statistician, statistical, biostatistics.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 statistics、statistic、statistician、statistical、biostatistics。

normal.en: Fixed phrases carry the sense: statistically significant, statistically indistinguishable, statistically speaking.
normal.cn: 固定搭配承载词义：统计显著、统计上无法区分、从统计角度来说。

normal.en: A result can be statistically real and still too small to matter.
normal.cn: 结果可以在统计上真实存在，却仍小到不重要。

normal.en: Statistically answers 'by what measure?', not 'how much?'
normal.cn: statistically 回答「用什么度量判断」，而不是「有多少」。

abstract.en: Picture two curves lying inside the same error band.
abstract.cn: 想象两条曲线落在同一条误差带里。

abstract.en: Picture a coin flipped a thousand times instead of once.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚硬币被掷一千次，而不是一次。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler whose smallest mark is labelled 'not enough evidence'.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺子，最小的刻度标着「证据不足」。

examples.en: Statistically, the two schools differ by less than one point.
examples.cn: 从统计上看，两所学校的差距不到一分。

examples.en: The treatment worked statistically, though few patients noticed a change.
examples.cn: 该疗法在统计上有效，尽管很少有病人感到变化。

examples.en: Statistically speaking, the risk rises sharply after the age of sixty.
examples.cn: 从统计角度来说，风险在六十岁之后急剧上升。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「statistical（统计的）+ ly」——拿数字说话 → statistically 从统计上看

root: 拉丁 status「国家、状态」（出自 stare「站立」）→ 新拉丁 statisticum → 德语 Statistik → 英语 statistics → statistical + -ly。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses cover the plain standpoint, the significance threshold, calculated odds, undetectable difference, representative sampling, discourse framing, the average case and practical negligibility.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项覆盖：一般统计立场、显著性门槛、计算出的概率、无法检出的差异、代表性抽样、话语框定、平均情形，以及实际可忽略性。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two results sit inside one error band, and the ruler decides whether they differ.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个结果落在同一条误差带里，由标尺决定它们是否不同。

branches.en: THE STANDPOINT: judge by data and method rather than by impression.
branches.cn: 立场：用数据与方法判断，而不是凭印象。

branches.en: THE SIGNIFICANCE LINE: the difference passes a pre-set chance test.
branches.cn: 显著性界线：差异通过了预设的偶然性检验。

branches.en: ODDS AND REPRESENTATION: probability read from a distribution, and a sample that mirrors it.
branches.cn: 概率与代表性：从分布读出的概率，以及与之相称的样本。

branches.en: LIMITS OF EVIDENCE: no detectable difference, and a framing phrase that admits exceptions.
branches.cn: 证据的限度：检不出差异，以及承认例外的框定说法。

branches.en: THE MIDDLE VERSUS THE TRIVIAL: the average case, and an effect too small to act on.
branches.cn: 中间情形与微不足道：平均情形，以及小到无需行动的效应。

intro.en: Statistically is a three-layer English word: statistics from German and New Latin, the adjective ending -al, and the native manner-adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: statistically 是三层构成的英语词：来自德语与新拉丁的 statistics，形容词词尾 -al，以及本族方式副词词尾 -ly。

latinIntro.en: The Latin element is status 'state, condition', from stare 'to stand', carried into New Latin statisticum and then into German and English.
latinIntro.cn: 其中的拉丁成分是 status「国家、状况」，出自 stare「站立」，经新拉丁 statisticum 进入德语与英语。

items.example: The groups did not differ statistically.
items.exampleCN: 各组在统计上没有差异。

items.example: The survey has a statistical appendix.
items.exampleCN: 该调查附有统计附录。

items.structure: German Statistik, from New Latin statisticum
items.example: Statistics is required for the degree.
items.exampleCN: 该学位要求修统计学。

items.example: Goals per game is a useful statistic.
items.exampleCN: 每场进球数是一项有用的统计量。

items.example: The statistician questioned the sample size.
items.exampleCN: 统计学家质疑样本量。

items.example: The coach checked the stats at halftime.
items.exampleCN: 教练在半场时查看了数据。

items.meaningCN: 用于生命系统的统计学
items.example: Biostatistics sets the rules for trial analysis.
items.exampleCN: 生物统计学为试验分析设定规则。

items.meaning: the probability threshold for a result
items.meaningCN: 结果所通过的概率门槛
items.example: The finding reached statistical significance.
items.exampleCN: 该发现达到统计显著。

definition_zh: 可证伪的；能被证明为假的；可被反证推翻的；（科学哲学）具备可检验性的
definition_en: capable of being proved false, especially by an observation or test that contradicts the claim
core_image: 一张写着预言的纸被一只手指按住，旁边摆着一台能显示否定结果的仪器
scene: 会议上有人提出一条断言，随后又补充说明哪种观测结果会让他当场认错。 A claim becomes falsifiable once its author names the observation that would prove it wrong.
sceneCN: 这里指一种说法有被事实推翻的可能（第 1 个义项：可被证明为假）；句意为当提出者说出了哪种观测能证明自己错时，这个说法才成为可证伪的。场景图取象：预言旁摆着一台能给出否定结果的仪器。

pos.zh: 可证伪的；能被证明为假的
（科学哲学）具备可检验性的，即存在可能的反例
（一般用法）可被质疑、可被推翻的

derivatives.zh: 证伪；伪造（由「假」与「做」合成，字面即「使之为假」）
可证伪性（在可证伪的形容词后加表示「性质」的名词后缀，是科学哲学的核心标准）
证伪；伪造（加表示「行为、过程」的拉丁后缀）
不可证伪的（加表示否定的前缀，指任何观测都无法推翻）
证伪者（加表示「施动者」的名词后缀）

senses.title: Open to being proved wrong
senses.definition: capable of being shown false by evidence that contradicts the claim
senses.definitionCN: 能够被与主张相抵触的证据证明为假
senses.example: A good forecast is falsifiable by the weather itself.
senses.exampleCN: 一个像样的预报能被天气本身证明为错。
senses.why: The suffix means 'can be', so the adjective simply says the claim is able to be made false.
senses.whyCN: 这个词尾意为「能够被」，因此这个形容词只是说该主张有可能被做成假的。

senses.title: The mark of a science
senses.definition: in Popper's method, framed so that some observable event would count against the theory
senses.definitionCN: 在波普尔的方法中，其表述方式使某种可观测事件足以对该理论不利
senses.example: Astrology is not falsifiable in the way astronomy is.
senses.exampleCN: 占星术不像天文学那样可证伪。
senses.why: The criterion is not truth but risk: a theory must be able to lose before it can win.
senses.whyCN: 标准不在真假而在风险：理论得先能输，才有资格赢。

senses.title: Testable by observation
senses.definition: stated in terms specific enough that observation could confirm or deny it
senses.definitionCN: 表述足够具体，使观测能够确认或否定它
senses.example: The prediction was falsifiable because it named a date and a place.
senses.exampleCN: 这个预测可证伪，因为它点明了日期和地点。
senses.why: Specificity is what gives a test something to bite on; vagueness protects a claim from being refuted.
senses.whyCN: 具体性给了检验可咬住的东西；含糊则让主张免于被驳倒。

senses.title: Exposed to challenge
senses.definition: in everyday use, open to challenge or contradiction by others
senses.definitionCN: 在日常用法中，可被他人质疑或反驳
senses.example: Her proposal was falsifiable, so the committee could argue with it.
senses.exampleCN: 她的提案可被反驳，委员会因此能就它争论。
senses.why: Outside the laboratory, the word means a claim that accepts opposition rather than silencing it.
senses.whyCN: 在实验室之外，这个词指一种肯接受反对、而不封杀反对的说法。

senses.title: Can be invalidated by a counterexample
senses.definition: in logic, able to be proved invalid by a single counterexample
senses.definitionCN: 在逻辑中，能被单独一个反例证明为无效
senses.example: The rule was falsifiable by one awkward case.
senses.exampleCN: 这条规则被一个棘手的例子就能推翻。
senses.why: A general rule claims all cases without exception, so one exception is enough to break it.
senses.whyCN: 通则宣称毫无例外地覆盖全部情形，一个例外就足以把它打破。

senses.title: A testable statistical prediction
senses.definition: expressed as a quantitative prediction that data could contradict
senses.definitionCN: 表述为数量化预测，使数据有可能与之相抵触
senses.example: The model's projection was falsifiable by next year's figures.
senses.exampleCN: 该模型的预测能被明年的数字证伪。
senses.why: Numbers give a prediction edges sharp enough for data to cut against.
senses.whyCN: 数字把预测磨出锋刃，数据才割得进去。

senses.title: Not the same as false
senses.definition: standing in contrast with 'false': a falsifiable claim may in fact be true
senses.definitionCN: 与「假」相对照：可证伪的说法事实上也可能是真的
senses.example: The statement is falsifiable but happens to be true.
senses.exampleCN: 这个陈述可证伪，却恰好为真。
senses.why: Being able to lose and having lost are different states, a distinction students often blur.
senses.whyCN: 「能输」与「已经输了」是两种状态，学生常把这一区别抹平。

senses.title: Designed to be refutable
senses.definition: of an experiment or study, set up so that a negative outcome is possible and informative
senses.definitionCN: 指实验或研究的设计使否定结果既有可能出现，又能说明问题
senses.example: The team built a falsifiable test instead of a demonstration.
senses.exampleCN: 团队建的是一个可证伪的检验，而不是一场演示。
senses.why: An experiment that cannot fail teaches nothing, which is why the adjective attaches to design.
senses.whyCN: 不会失败的实验什么也教不了，所以这个形容词常挂在设计上。

intro.en: Falsifiable is falsify plus the Latin suffix -abilis, 'able to be'. The word itself is old; its special sense as a test of science comes from Popper in the 1930s.
intro.cn: falsifiable 是 falsify 加拉丁语词尾 -abilis「能够被……」构成。词本身并不新，它作为科学检验标准的特殊含义来自二十世纪三十年代的波普尔。

items.en: The base verb falsify joins falsus 'false' with facere 'to make', so it means to make false or to show false.
items.cn: 基础动词 falsify 把 falsus「假」与 facere「做」合起来，意为使假或证明为假。

items.en: Latin -abilis forms adjectives of capability, the same ending that gives readable and breakable in English.
items.cn: 拉丁语 -abilis 构成表示能力的形容词，英语里的 readable 与 breakable 用的正是同一词尾。

items.en: The adjective appears in English well before modern science, simply meaning able to be shown false.
items.cn: 这个形容词远在现代科学之前就出现在英语里，意思只是「能被证明为假」。

items.en: Karl Popper made falsifiability the dividing line between scientific and non-scientific claims in his logic of research.
items.cn: 波普尔在他的研究逻辑中，把可证伪性立为科学主张与非科学主张的分界线。

items.en: The English edition of 1959 carried the term into ordinary scientific speech, where it has stayed.
items.cn: 一九五九年的英译本把这个术语带入日常的科学语言，此后一直沿用。

items.en: Recent debates about replication gave new life to the adjective, now applied to data and methods as well as theories.
items.cn: 近年关于可重复性的争论给这个形容词注入新生命，如今它也被用于数据与方法，而不只是理论。

note.en: The first group shares the false-making root or looks close; the second group holds words that describe testability, which is often mistaken for falsifiability.
note.cn: 第一组或共享「使假」词根，或字形相近；第二组描述可检验性，常被误当作可证伪性。

entries.definition: The verb: to prove false or to make a record false.
entries.definitionCN: 动词：证明为假，或把记录做假。

entries.definition: The act of proving false, or the doctoring of records.
entries.definitionCN: 证明为假的行为，或对记录的篡改。

entries.definition: The noun for the property the adjective names.
entries.definitionCN: 指这个形容词所述性质的名词。

entries.definition: Able to be mistaken, said of people rather than claims.
entries.definitionCN: 会犯错的，用于人而非主张。

entries.definition: Practicable; it shares the -ible shape but comes from a root meaning to do or make readily.
entries.definitionCN: 可行的；词尾形状相同，词根却意为易于做成。

entries.definition: Able to be checked by experiment, which is necessary but not sufficient for falsifiability.
entries.definitionCN: 能用实验检查，这是可证伪的必要条件，却并不充分。

entries.definition: Able to be proved wrong by argument, the word used of statements rather than theories.
entries.definitionCN: 能被论证驳倒，多用于陈述而非理论。

entries.definition: Able to be shown false by evidence, the plain English equivalent.
entries.definitionCN: 能被证据证明为假，是最朴素的英语对应词。

entries.definition: Beyond any possible test, and therefore outside science by Popper's rule.
entries.definitionCN: 超出任何可能的检验，按波普尔的规则因此落在科学之外。

entries.definition: Able to be shown true; the optimistic twin of the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 能被证明为真；是这个形容词乐观的另一半。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real suffix, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实词尾、真实同族词与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: The ending -able means can be, so falsifiable is can be made false.
normal.cn: 词尾意为「能够被」，可证伪就是能够被做成假的。

normal.en: Falsify is false plus make, and the same ending builds readable and breakable.
normal.cn: 基础动词是「假」加「做」，同一词尾还造出可读的与易碎的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: falsifiable hypothesis, falsifiable prediction, not falsifiable.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出用法：可证伪的假说、可证伪的预测、不可证伪。

normal.en: The opposite is unfalsifiable, which is a criticism rather than a compliment in science.
normal.cn: 反义词是不可证伪，在科学里这是批评而非称赞。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with false: a falsifiable claim can still be true.
normal.cn: 别把它当作「假」：可证伪的说法仍可能是真的。

abstract.en: Falsifiable means a claim has left itself a door through which it could be thrown out.
abstract.cn: 可证伪意味着一个说法给自己留了一扇门，好让人能把它扔出去。

abstract.en: The adjective measures courage in an idea, not correctness.
abstract.cn: 这个形容词衡量的是一个想法的勇气，而不是它的正确。

abstract.en: A claim that can lose is already taking part in the world it describes.
abstract.cn: 一个能输的说法，已经参与到它所描述的世界里了。

examples.en: A falsifiable claim states what would count against it.
examples.cn: 可证伪的主张会说明什么结果对它不利。

examples.en: The hypothesis was falsifiable but never actually falsified.
examples.cn: 这个假说可证伪，却从未真的被证伪。

examples.en: Models that are not falsifiable tend to survive for the wrong reason.
examples.cn: 不可证伪的模型往往因为错误的理由而存活。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「佛西法伊额波」——能被做成假的，就是能被推翻的：可证伪的

root: falsify ＋ 拉丁语形容词词尾 -abilis「能够被……」；falsify 出自晚期拉丁语 falsificare，由 falsus「假」＋ facere「做」构成。作为科学哲学的关键标准，源自波普尔一九三〇年代的著作，一九五九年英译本使其通行。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all circle one property: a claim that could be shown wrong, whether by a named observation, a counterexample, a statistical result, or an experiment built to fail.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都围绕一种性质：一个可能被证明为错的说法，无论靠点明的观测、一个反例、一组统计结果，还是一场存心设计得可能失败的实验。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a prediction with a trapdoor built in, through which a contrary fact could drop it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条为自己装好翻板的预言，相反的事实可以从那里把它放下去。

branches.en: THE OPEN CLAIM: able to be shown false, yet not itself false.
branches.cn: 留了门的主张：能被证明为假，却不是假。

branches.en: THE RISKY TEST: a study or theory framed so that losing is possible and informative.
branches.cn: 有风险的检验：研究或理论的设计使失败既可能出现，又能说明问题。

branches.en: THE SPECIFIC PREDICTION: a date, place or figure sharp enough for data to contradict.
branches.cn: 具体的预测：日期、地点或数字足够明确，数据才反驳得动。

branches.en: THE PUBLIC CHALLENGE: in ordinary speech, a proposal that accepts argument.
branches.cn: 公开的质疑：在日常言语里，指肯接受争论的提案。

branches.en: THE ONE EXCEPTION: logic lets a single awkward case invalidate a general rule.
branches.cn: 那一个例外：逻辑允许一个棘手的例子使通则失效。

intro.en: Falsifiable is a Latin verb plus a Latin capability suffix, a pattern shared by hundreds of English adjectives.
intro.cn: falsifiable 是一个拉丁动词加一个表示能力的拉丁词尾，这一模式在英语形容词里很常见。

latinIntro.en: The pieces are falsus, facere and -abilis, all with clear histories.
latinIntro.cn: 构件为 falsus、facere 与 -abilis，来源都清楚。

items.meaning: able to be made or shown false
items.example: The adjective is the standard term in method.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词是方法论中的标准术语。

items.meaning: to make false; to prove false
items.example: The verb keeps both directions of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词保留了这个词的两个方向。

items.example: It also gives false and falsity.
items.exampleCN: 它还给出 false 与 falsity。

items.example: It supplies the -fy ending.
items.exampleCN: 它提供 -fy 词尾。

items.example: It builds readable, breakable and falsifiable.
items.exampleCN: 它构成可读的、易碎的与可证伪的。

items.example: It turns the adjective into a noun of property.
items.exampleCN: 它把这个形容词变成性质名词。

items.example: It builds unfalsifiable, the word used against bad science.
items.exampleCN: 它构成不可证伪，即用来批评坏科学之词。

items.example: It builds falsification from falsify.
items.exampleCN: 它把 falsify 变成证伪这一名词。

latinEntries.example: The Latin verb is the base of the English adjective.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词是英语形容词的词基。

latinEntries.structure: Latin adjective falsus (false), participle of fallere
latinEntries.example: Latin falsus means false, and gives English false.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 falsus 意为假的，并给出英语 false。

latinEntries.example: Latin -abilis builds adjectives such as demonstrabilis.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 -abilis 构成 demonstrabilis（可证明的）这类形容词。

definition_zh: 引起；引发；导致；使……产生；催生
definition_en: to cause something to begin or to appear, often something unintended, indirect or far-reaching
core_image: 一颗小石子落进静水，第一圈波纹很小，第二圈更大，后面的波纹一路推到池边
scene: 编辑在稿件页边画满问号，因为一句措辞含糊的话可能引出许多不必要的争论。 One careless sentence may give rise to a long dispute over meaning.
sceneCN: 这里指引发、使某事开始（第 1 个义项：使争论或问题由此产生）；句意为一句不小心的措辞可能引发一场关于含义的长期争论。图中可辨识物件：稿件、页边问号、红笔、校样。

pos.zh: 引起；引发（及物动词短语，宾语多为问题、争论、现象）
催生；使产生（宾语可为新事物、新领域）

collocations.phrase: give rise to a new field

derivatives.zh: 短语中的核心名词兼动词，义为「上升；升起；兴起」
由动词加分词词尾构成，义为「上升的；上升」
核心动词的过去分词形式
由给予动词加施事词尾构成，义为「给予者」，与本短语关系较远

senses.title: Start a dispute
senses.definition: to cause an argument or a debate to begin
senses.definitionCN: 使争论或辩论开始
senses.example: The ambiguous clause may give rise to years of argument.
senses.exampleCN: 这条含糊的条款可能引发多年的争论。
senses.why: Rise is the moment something lifts off the ground; a dispute given rise is one that has left silence and started to move.
senses.whyCN: 「升起」是某物离开地面的那一刻；被「升起」的争论，就是离开沉默开始动起来的那一场。

senses.title: Cause an illness
senses.definition: to bring about a health problem or an outbreak
senses.definitionCN: 造成健康问题或疾病爆发
senses.example: Standing water can give rise to a mosquito problem.
senses.exampleCN: 积水可能引发蚊虫问题。
senses.why: Standing water lets a problem rise and spread beyond its own edge.
senses.whyCN: 积水让问题升起，并越过自己的边缘扩散。

senses.title: Produce a new field
senses.definition: to cause a new branch of study or practice to appear
senses.definitionCN: 使新的研究或实践分支出现
senses.example: Cheap sequencing can give rise to a new branch of ecology.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价的测序技术可以催生生态学的一个新分支。
senses.why: A method lets a new branch of study rise where none stood before.
senses.whyCN: 一种方法让新的研究分支在原本空无处升起。

senses.title: Arouse doubt
senses.definition: to cause uncertainty about a claim or a record
senses.definitionCN: 使人们对某个说法或记录产生不确定
senses.example: The missing page may give rise to doubt about the whole ledger.
senses.exampleCN: 缺失的那一页可能使人们对整本账簿产生怀疑。
senses.why: A missing page lets uncertainty rise about everything after it.
senses.whyCN: 缺了一页，怀疑就在其后的一切上升起。

senses.title: Lead to litigation
senses.definition: to cause legal action to be brought
senses.definitionCN: 使法律诉讼被提起
senses.example: A vague contract can give rise to costly disputes.
senses.exampleCN: 一份含糊的合同可能引发代价高昂的纠纷。
senses.why: A vague clause lets a dispute rise into the courts.
senses.whyCN: 含糊条款让纠纷升进法庭。

senses.title: Cause misunderstanding
senses.definition: to produce a false impression in someone's mind
senses.definitionCN: 在他人心中造成错误的印象
senses.example: A literal translation may give rise to a false impression.
senses.exampleCN: 逐字直译可能造成错误的印象。
senses.why: A literal rendering lets a wrong picture rise in the reader's mind.
senses.whyCN: 逐字直译让错误画面在读者心里升起。

senses.title: Create an industry
senses.definition: to cause a cluster of businesses to form
senses.definitionCN: 使一群相关企业形成
senses.example: The new port can give rise to a cluster of repair shops.
senses.exampleCN: 新港口可以催生一群修船作坊。
senses.why: A port lets a cluster of workshops rise beside it.
senses.whyCN: 港口让一群作坊在它旁边升起。

senses.title: Set off a chain reaction
senses.definition: to start a sequence of effects that feed on one another
senses.definitionCN: 启动一连串彼此推动的后果
senses.example: One dry summer may give rise to a wave of beetle damage.
senses.exampleCN: 一个干旱的夏天可能引发一波甲虫危害。
senses.why: One dry summer lets a wave of damage rise and feed on itself.
senses.whyCN: 一个旱夏让一波损害升起并自我喂养。

senses.title: Stir an emotion
senses.definition: to cause a feeling to arise in someone
senses.definitionCN: 使某种感受在某人心中升起
senses.example: The photograph can give rise to a strong sense of loss.
senses.exampleCN: 那张照片可以引发强烈的失落感。
senses.why: A photograph lets a feeling rise that had settled out of sight.
senses.whyCN: 一张照片让沉到看不见处的感受重新升起。

intro.en: The phrase joins the native verb of giving to the native noun of rising. The cause is pictured as a hand that lets something go up, and what goes up then spreads on its own.
intro.cn: 这个短语把本族表示「给予」的动词与本族表示「升起」的名词结合。原因被画成一只放手让某物升起的手，而升起之物随后自行扩散。

items.en: Giefan meant to give, to grant, and it is one of the oldest verbs in the language.
items.cn: 这个词意为「给予、授予」，是语言中最古老的动词之一。

items.en: Risan meant to rise, to get up, to move upward, and it stands behind the modern noun and verb.
items.cn: 这个词意为「升起、起身、向上移动」，现代的名词与动词都由它而来。

items.en: The combination appears in the seventeenth century, first for physical beginnings and soon for disputes and doubts.
items.cn: 这个组合在十七世纪出现，先指物理上的开始，很快用于争论与怀疑。

items.en: Unlike a direct maker, the phrase often names a small trigger whose effects grow on their own; this is why it suits unintended problems.
items.cn: 与直接的制造者不同，这个短语常指一个小小触发点，其后果自行扩大；这正是它适合「非本意问题」的原因。

items.en: The exact first citation of the phrase is uncertain, and the deeper origin of the rising verb is a reconstructed form rather than a recorded one.
items.cn: 该短语最早的书证年代不确定；表示「升起」的动词更早的来源属重构形式，并非有记录的原形。

note.en: The first group shares the giving or rising words in other combinations; the second group holds other verbs of causing, including the one most often confused with this phrase.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「给予」或「升起」之词的其他组合；第二组是其他表示「造成」的动词，其中包含最易与本短语混淆的一个。

entries.definition: The bare verb takes a concrete object, as give a book; the phrase takes an event or a condition that begins.
entries.definitionCN: 单独使用时带具体宾语，如给一本书；短语的宾语则是开始的事件或状况。

entries.definition: Alone it names the upward movement itself, not the cause that started it.
entries.definitionCN: 单独使用时指「上升」这一运动本身，而不指启动它的原因。

entries.definition: It means to yield or to be replaced by something, not to cause something to begin.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「让位、被取代」，而不是「使某物开始」。

entries.definition: It means to stop trying or to surrender, with no causal sense at all.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「放弃、投降」，完全不含因果义。

entries.definition: It stresses a cause that carries a result into fact, and it suits deliberate reforms; the phrase here leans toward indirect or unintended effects.
entries.definitionCN: 强调把结果搬进事实，适合有意的改革；本短语则偏向间接或非本意的后果。

entries.definition: It follows a path toward a result and stresses the sequence rather than the first spark.
entries.definitionCN: 沿一条路径通向结果，强调过程顺序而非最初的火花。

entries.definition: A vivid verb for a small action that sets off a large reaction, close to the eighth sense.
entries.definitionCN: 形象地表示小动作引发大反应，接近第八个义项。

entries.definition: It takes the outcome as its object and looks backward from the result, not forward from the cause.
entries.definitionCN: 以结果为宾语，从结果往回看，而不是从原因往前看。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the pebble and the pond, the standing water, the new port and the old photograph.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用石子与池塘、积水、新港口与旧照片四个场景。

normal.en: A pebble dropped into still water: one small ring, then wider ones reaching the edge.
normal.cn: 石子落进静水：先一圈小波纹，随后更大的波纹一路推到池边。

normal.en: A puddle behind a wall that becomes a mosquito nursery.
normal.cn: 墙后的一摊积水，成了蚊子的育婴房。

normal.en: A new port, and a row of repair shops opening beside it.
normal.cn: 新港口开张，旁边跟着开了一排修船铺。

normal.en: A page missing from a ledger, and every later entry doubted.
normal.cn: 账簿少了一页，后面的每一条都变得可疑。

normal.en: A photograph that brings back a loss one had stopped feeling daily.
normal.cn: 一张照片，把早已不再天天想起的失去又带了回来。

abstract.en: A rise is a beginning that keeps going after the hand is gone.
abstract.cn: 升起，是手松开之后仍然继续的开始。

abstract.en: Small causes with long wakes are the hardest kind to trace back.
abstract.cn: 小原因拖出长尾迹，最难回溯。

abstract.en: The phrase never says the cause was intended, which is why it fits accidents and discoveries alike.
abstract.cn: 这个短语从不交代原因是否有意，因此事故与发现都适用。

examples.en: A single ambiguous word may give rise to two opposite readings.
examples.cn: 一个含义模糊的词，可能引出两种相反的理解。

examples.en: Rapid irrigation can give rise to salt buildup in the soil.
examples.cn: 快速灌溉可能引起土壤盐分累积。

examples.en: The discovery may give rise to a whole new class of materials.
examples.cn: 这一发现可能催生一整类新材料。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「基夫 赖兹 图」：把「让某物升起」记成石子落水，第一圈很小，后面的波纹自己推到岸边——这就是引发

root: 前半为本族动词，意为「给予、授予」；后半为本族名词，意为「升起、兴起」。短语整体把原因画成一只放手让某物升起的手，强调后果自行扩散，不交代是否有意为之。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses let something rise: a dispute, a disease, a field, a doubt, a lawsuit, a misunderstanding, an industry, a chain of damage, and a feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项让某物升起：争论、疾病、学科、怀疑、诉讼、误解、产业、连锁损害与情感。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pebble dropped into still water, a small first ring, then wider rings travelling to the edge of the pool.
core.cn: 核心意象：石子落进静水，第一圈很小，随后更大的波纹一路推到池边。

branches.en: THE PUBLIC CLASH: a clause starts an argument, a vague contract starts a lawsuit.
branches.cn: 公开的冲突：一条条款引起争论，一份含糊合同引起诉讼。

branches.en: THE GROWING WAKE: standing water breeds mosquitoes, a dry summer feeds a beetle wave.
branches.cn: 扩大的尾迹：积水养蚊，旱夏养甲虫。

branches.en: THE NEW THING: a method opens a field, a port opens a cluster of shops.
branches.cn: 新生之物：一种方法开出一门学科，一个港口开出一群作坊。

branches.en: THE DOUBTFUL MIND: a missing page and a literal translation both plant a wrong picture.
branches.cn: 起疑的心：缺页与直译，都在心里种下错误的画面。

branches.en: THE STIRRED FEELING: a photograph raises a loss that had gone quiet.
branches.cn: 被搅动的情感：一张照片让沉寂的失去重新升起。

intro.en: Both halves are native English, so the family is short and concrete: a giving verb, a rising verb, and their forms.
intro.cn: 两部分都是本族英语，因此词族短而具体：一个「给予」动词、一个「升起」动词及其形式。

latinIntro.en: No Latin source is involved in either half, so the Latin list is left empty and the native forms are given instead.
latinIntro.cn: 两部分都不涉及拉丁语来源，因此拉丁词表留空，改列本族形式。

items.example: The second half of the phrase.

items.exampleCN: 升起动词最古老的记录形式。

items.exampleCN: 它标出现在时的单数主语。

items.example: It forms the participle of the phrase.
items.exampleCN: 它构成短语的现在分词。

items.example: The giving verb keeps an old strong form.
items.exampleCN: 给予动词保留了古老的强变化形式。

items.example: It points the rise at what is produced.
items.exampleCN: 它把「升起」指向所产生之物。

由分词转作形容词，义为「上升的」
由给予动词加施事词尾构成，义为「给予者」

definition_zh: 开发利用；资源开采；商业开发；剥削；利用；漏洞利用
definition_en: the act of using a resource, situation or person for profit or advantage, whether fairly and productively or unfairly and at their expense
core_image: 一座山被层层剥开，矿石装上卡车运走，山脚下的人只拿到很少的报酬
scene: 矿区的老照片挂在会议室墙上，一边是装满矿石的卡车，一边是被挖空的山体。 The company's exploitation of the local iron ore lasted forty years.
sceneCN: 这里指对自然资源的开采利用（第 1 个义项：资源开发利用）；句意为这家公司对当地铁矿的开发持续了四十年。图中可辨识物件：露天矿坑、运矿卡车、山体剖面、会议室照片墙。

pos.zh: 开发利用；资源开采；剥削；利用

derivatives.zh: 同一词干构成的动词与名词，义为「开发利用；剥削」与「功绩」
由动词加表示施动者的名词尾构成，义为「开发者；剥削者」
由动词加表示性质的形容词尾构成，义为「剥削性的」
由动词加表示「可……的」形容词尾构成，义为「可利用的」
由表示「过度」的前缀加本词构成，义为「过度开发」

senses.title: Productive use of natural resources
senses.definition: the working of land, minerals, water or forests for economic benefit
senses.definitionCN: 对土地、矿产、水源或森林进行有经济收益的开发利用
senses.example: The company's exploitation of the local iron ore lasted forty years.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司对当地铁矿的开发持续了四十年。
senses.why: The oldest sense is a deed carried out and brought to profit, so working a mine counts as an exploit before it counts as abuse.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的含义是「做成一件事并从中获利」，因此开采矿山先被算作一番作为，之后才被算作剥削。

senses.title: Commercial development of an idea or market
senses.definition: the turning of an invention, brand or market into a source of revenue
senses.definitionCN: 把发明、品牌或市场变成收入来源
senses.example: Critics said the film was a commercial exploitation of a true story.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者说这部电影是对一个真实故事的商业开发。
senses.why: When the resource is an idea or a market rather than a mine, the same word means packaging it for sale.
senses.whyCN: 当被开发的对象从矿山变成创意或市场，同一个词就指把它包装出售。

senses.title: Use of data or personal information
senses.titleCN: 数据与个人信息的利用
senses.definition: the collection and use of data, often without the clear consent of the people concerned
senses.definitionCN: 收集并使用数据，且常常没有获得当事人的明确同意
senses.example: The inquiry examined the exploitation of user data by the platform.
senses.exampleCN: 调查审查了该平台对用户数据的使用。
senses.why: Data became a resource in the digital economy, and the word followed the resource.
senses.whyCN: 在数字经济中数据成了资源，这个词也就跟着资源走。

senses.title: Unfair use of labour
senses.definition: the payment of very little for long or hard work while another party keeps the profit
senses.definitionCN: 以极低报酬换取长时间或高强度劳动，利润归他方所有
senses.example: Inspectors found exploitation of migrant workers on the construction site.
senses.exampleCN: 检查人员发现工地上存在对移民工人的剥削。
senses.why: Here the thing being worked is a person, and the profit is taken from their hours and body.
senses.whyCN: 这里被「开发」的对象是人，利润取自他们的工时与身体。

senses.title: Taking advantage of generosity
senses.definition: the use of someone's kindness, trust or weakness for one's own benefit
senses.definitionCN: 利用他人的善意、信任或弱点为自己谋利
senses.example: He described the loan as an exploitation of his father's generosity.
senses.exampleCN: 他把这笔借款说成是对父亲善意的利用。
senses.why: No mine and no market are needed: a human weakness is the seam being excavated.
senses.whyCN: 既不需要矿山也不需要市场：被开采的矿脉是人的弱点。

senses.title: Abuse of a vulnerable group
senses.definition: a systematic taking of value from people who cannot refuse, such as children or the poor
senses.definitionCN: 从无法拒绝的人身上系统性地榨取价值，如儿童或穷人
senses.example: The report documented exploitation of children in the informal economy.
senses.exampleCN: 报告记录了大量非正规经济中对儿童的剥削。
senses.why: The word turns from individual meanness to a structure when the group itself has no power to say no.
senses.whyCN: 当整个群体没有拒绝的能力时，这个词就从个人的刻薄变成一种结构。

senses.title: Extraction beyond renewal
senses.titleCN: 超出再生能力的过度攫取
senses.definition: harvesting or extraction at a rate faster than a natural system can recover
senses.definitionCN: 采伐或捕捞的速度快过自然系统的恢复能力
senses.example: Over-exploitation of the fishery left the boats with empty nets.
senses.exampleCN: 对渔场的过度捕捞让渔船空手而归。
senses.why: The prefix of excess turns the same act into one that destroys its own resource.
senses.whyCN: 表示「过度」的前缀把同一行为变成毁掉自身资源的行为。

senses.title: Use of a technical flaw
senses.definition: the deliberate use of a weakness in software or a system to gain access or control
senses.definitionCN: 故意利用软件或系统中的弱点取得访问权或控制权
senses.example: The attack began with exploitation of an unpatched browser flaw.
senses.exampleCN: 这次攻击始于对一个未修补的浏览器漏洞的利用。
senses.why: A loophole is a resource too: security language borrowed the word for a hole opened on purpose.
senses.whyCN: 漏洞也是一种资源：安全领域借用了这个词，指一个被故意打开的缺口。

senses.title: Full use of an opportunity
senses.definition: the energetic use of a chance or advantage that is legitimately available
senses.definitionCN: 对一个正当可用的机会或优势加以充分利用
senses.example: The coach praised the team's exploitation of every scoring chance.
senses.exampleCN: 教练称赞球队充分利用了每一次得分机会。
senses.why: The neutral sense survives in sport and business, where using an opening well is simply good play.
senses.whyCN: 这个中性含义在体育与商业中留存：把空档用好，本身就是好球。

intro.en: Exploitation goes back to a Latin verb meaning to unfold, through French a deed or a profit, and then to the modern sense of working a resource.
intro.cn: 这个词可追到拉丁语表示「展开」的动词，经法语表示「作为、获利」，再到现代「开发资源」的含义。

items.en: plicare meant to fold, and its compounds describe bending something into layers.
items.cn: plicare 意为「折叠」，其复合词描述把某物折成层。

items.en: ex- plus plicare gave explicare, to unfold or set out in order.
items.cn: 表示「向外」的前缀加「折叠」，构成 explicare，意为「展开、摊开说明」。

items.en: The participle explicitum named something unfolded and therefore made clear.
items.cn: 分词形式 explicitum 指被展开、因而变得清楚的事物。

items.en: French turned the idea into esploit, a deed accomplished, and later a source of profit.
items.cn: 法语把这一意思变成 esploit，指做成的一番作为，后来指利润来源。

items.en: English first used the deed word as exploit and built exploitation on it; the first records cluster in the early modern period and the exact date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语先把「作为」这个词用作 exploit，再由此构成 exploitation；首见记录集中出现在近代早期，具体年份不确定。

items.en: Industrial mining and factory labour gave the noun its double life as resource development and human abuse.
items.cn: 工业化采矿与工厂劳动让这个名词有了双面人生：资源开发与对人的剥削。

note.en: The first group shares form or root with exploitation; the second group names nearby ideas of using something for gain.
note.cn: 第一组在形音或词根上与 exploitation 相近；第二组是与「为获利而使用」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The verb to develop a resource or take unfair advantage of a person, and the noun for a bold deed.
entries.definitionCN: 指开发资源或对人占便宜的动词，也指「壮举」的名词。

entries.definition: A person or firm that works a resource or takes advantage of others.
entries.definitionCN: 指开发资源的个人或企业，或占他人便宜的人。

entries.definition: Describing a relationship or practice that extracts value unfairly.
entries.definitionCN: 形容不公平榨取价值的关系或做法。

entries.definition: The search for resources or knowledge; it looks close but comes from a verb meaning to search out, not to unfold.
entries.definitionCN: 指对资源或知识的勘探与探索；形近，但来自表示「搜寻」而非「展开」的动词。

entries.definition: Stated fully and leaving nothing folded away; it shares the unfolding image.
entries.definitionCN: 指表述完整、毫不含糊；与本词共享「展开」的意象。

entries.definition: The process of bringing land, resources or ideas into productive use; neutral and often positive.
entries.definitionCN: 指把土地、资源或想法带入生产用途的过程；中性且常为正面。

entries.definition: The effective use of something available; it stresses use, not profit or harm.
entries.definitionCN: 指对可用之物的有效使用；强调使用，不强调获利或伤害。

entries.definition: The wrong or harmful use of a power, substance or person; it stresses harm rather than extraction.
entries.definitionCN: 指对权力、物质或人的错误有害使用；强调伤害而非榨取。

entries.definition: Taking plants, fish or animals faster than they can replenish; the ecological twin of over-exploitation.
entries.definitionCN: 指对植物、鱼或动物的捕捞采集快于其补充；是「过度开发」的生态学说法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin image of unfolding, the real French deed word and the real resource-and-labour pairs.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁「展开」意象、真实的法语「作为」词，以及真实的资源与劳动搭配。

normal.en: The root picture is unfolding: a mine is land unfolded and spread out for profit.
normal.cn: 词根的意象是「展开」：矿山就是被摊开来换钱的土地。

normal.en: French esploit meant a deed done; exploitation is that deed turned into a business.
normal.cn: 法语 esploit 指做成一件事；exploitation 就是这件作为变成了生意。

normal.en: The same word covers a mine and a worker because both are seams someone works.
normal.cn: 同一个词既指矿山又指工人，因为两者都是被人开采的矿脉。

normal.en: Resource exploitation and labour exploitation sit on one page of the dictionary.
normal.cn: 资源开发与劳动剥削在词典的同一页上。

normal.en: Data is the new seam: data exploitation repeats the mining image.
normal.cn: 数据是新的矿脉：数据利用重复了采矿的意象。

abstract.en: Exploitation begins when a thing with its own life is seen only as something to be taken from.
abstract.cn: 剥削始于把一个有自己的生命的东西，只看成可供取用之物。

abstract.en: The word is neutral until the second party cannot say no; then development becomes extraction.
abstract.cn: 这个词本中性，直到另一方无法说不，开发就变成了榨取。

abstract.en: Every loophole is a small hole opened on purpose, which is why security borrowed the mining word.
abstract.cn: 每一个漏洞都是一个被故意打开的小口，所以安全领域借用了采矿的词。

examples.en: The treaty set limits on the exploitation of the river for hydropower.
examples.cn: 该条约对这条河的水电开发设定了限制。

examples.en: The court treated the long unpaid internships as exploitation of young workers.
examples.cn: 法院把长期无薪实习视为对年轻劳动者的剥削。

examples.en: Security teams patched the flaw before exploitation of it became widespread.
examples.cn: 安全团队在漏洞被广泛利用之前就完成了修补。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「爱克斯普洛伊泰申」——把矿藏「展开」摊开，再从中取利

root: 来自拉丁语 explicare「展开、摊开说明」← ex-「向外」+ plicare「折叠」，分词 explicitum 指「展开的」；经古法语 esploit「作为、获利」与法语 exploiter 进入英语，再由动词构成 exploitation。首见年代为约数，来源链清楚。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses move from working a mine, a market, data and a person to passing the limit and to two neutral uses in security and sport.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从开采矿山、开发市场、利用数据和剥削人，走到越过限度，最后落到安全与体育里两个中性用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hillside is unfolded layer by layer, ore goes one way and people stay at the pit edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：山坡被一层层展开，矿石被运走，人留在矿坑边缘。

branches.en: THE LAND AND THE MARKET: ore, land and ideas turned into revenue.
branches.cn: 土地与市场：矿石、土地与创意被换成收入。

branches.en: THE DATA SEAM: records mined for value, often without consent.
branches.cn: 数据矿脉：记录被开采出价值，常常未经同意。

branches.en: THE PERSON AS RESOURCE: hours, kindness and weakness turned into another's gain.
branches.cn: 把人当资源：工时、善意与弱点变成他人的收益。

branches.en: THE LIMIT PASSED: harvest that outruns renewal and destroys the seam.
branches.cn: 越过限度：收割快过再生，最终毁掉矿脉本身。

branches.en: THE OPEN HOLE: a system flaw or a brief chance used to the full.
branches.cn: 敞开的缺口：系统漏洞或短暂机会被充分利用。

intro.en: Exploitation is a verb stem plus a noun ending, with a Latin prefix and a Latin root still visible inside.
intro.cn: 这个词是动词词干加名词词尾，内部仍能看见一个拉丁前缀与一个拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies plicare and explicare, and the participle explicitum; French supplies the deed word exploit.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了 plicare、explicare 与分词 explicitum；法语提供了表示「作为」的 exploit。

items.example: It marks the unfolding outward.
items.exampleCN: 它标记「向外展开」。

items.example: The root names folded layers.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名折叠的层。

items.example: Prefix and root combine into the key verb.
items.exampleCN: 前缀与词根合成关键动词。

items.example: The participle supplies the clear sense.
items.exampleCN: 分词提供了「清楚」的含义。

items.example: It forms the English action noun.
items.exampleCN: 它构成英语的动作名词。

items.meaning: to work for gain; a bold deed
items.example: The base word keeps both sides.
items.exampleCN: 基础词兼含两面。

items.example: It forms exploiter, the one who works the seam.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 exploiter，指开采矿脉的人。

items.example: It forms exploitative, the unfair kind.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 exploitative，指剥削性的。

items.example: It forms exploitable, able to be used.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 exploitable，指可利用的。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加施动者词尾构成，义为「开发者；剥削者」
由动词加性质形容词尾构成，义为「剥削性的」
由动词加「可……的」形容词尾构成，义为「可利用的」
由「过度」前缀加本词构成，义为「过度开发」

definition_zh: 冰柜；冰箱冷冻室；冷藏库
definition_en: a machine or room used for keeping food frozen at a very low temperature
core_image: 一台低沉嗡嗡作响的柜子，门一开便涌出白雾，里面的食物冻得梆硬
scene: 清晨的厨房里，妈妈打开柜门取出一袋冻豆子，白雾扑面而来。 She took the last bag of peas out of the freezer.
sceneCN: 这里 freezer 是「冰柜；冷冻室」（第 1 个义项：低温冷冻食物的设备）；句意是她从冰柜里取出最后一袋豌豆。

pos.zh: 冰柜；冷冻室；冷藏库

collocations.phrase: take something out of the freezer
a chest freezer with a broken seal

derivatives.zh: 基础动词，义为「结冰；冷冻；冻结」，freezer 由其加名词后缀 -er 构成
freeze 的过去分词转形容词，义为「冰冻的；冷冻的」
freeze 加 -ing 构成，义为「极冷的；冰点以下的」

senses.title: A device that keeps food frozen
senses.definition: a household appliance or a compartment that stores food below freezing point
senses.definitionCN: 把食物储存在冰点以下的家用电器或冰箱的一个隔层
senses.example: The freezer hums quietly in the corner of the kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 冰柜在厨房角落里低声嗡嗡运转。
senses.why: The verb freeze names the action, and -er names the agent or tool that performs it.
senses.whyCN: 动词 freeze 表示「冷冻」这一动作，后缀 -er 表示执行该动作的工具。

senses.title: An industrial cold-storage room
senses.definition: a large room or storehouse where goods are kept at freezing temperatures
senses.definitionCN: 把货物保存在冷冻温度下的大房间或仓库
senses.example: Workers wear thick coats inside the meat freezer.
senses.exampleCN: 工人在肉类冷藏库里要穿上厚外套。
senses.why: The same tool-word scales up from a home appliance to an industrial chamber.
senses.whyCN: 同一个工具名词由家用电器放大为工业级冷冻库房。

senses.title: A stockpile of frozen food
senses.titleCN: 冻品储备；冰柜里的存粮
senses.definition: the supply of frozen food kept in such a device, spoken of as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 存放在冷冻设备里的冻品总量，被当作一个整体来谈论
senses.example: A well-stocked freezer saved us from cooking every night.
senses.exampleCN: 存满冻品的冰柜让我们不必每晚做饭。
senses.why: From naming the container, usage shifts to what the container holds.
senses.whyCN: 由指称容器转指容器所装之物，即冰柜里的冻品储备。

intro.en: Freezer is a modern agent noun: the old verb freeze plus the tool suffix -er.
intro.cn: freezer 是一个现代的工具名词：古老动词 freeze 加上工具后缀 -er。

items.en: The verb goes back to Proto-Germanic *frezaną, generally reconstructed as meaning to freeze, related to frost.
items.cn: 该动词可追溯至原始日耳曼语 *frezaną，一般认为重构义为「结冰」，与 frost（霜）同源。

items.en: Old English frēosan meant to freeze, used of water, weather, and people who felt cold.
items.cn: 古英语 frēosan 意为「结冰；冻僵」，既可用于水与天气，也可用于感到寒冷的人。

items.en: Middle English fresen kept the same core meaning and produced the past participle frozen.
items.cn: 中古英语 fresen 保持同一核心词义，并产生了过去分词 frozen。

items.en: With ice cutting and early refrigeration, agent nouns like freezer appeared for machines and cold rooms.
items.cn: 随着采冰业与早期制冷技术的出现，freezer 这类工具名词开始指机器与低温库房。

items.en: Electric household refrigeration made freezer a normal kitchen word, at first for the freezer compartment of a fridge.
items.cn: 家用电制冷的普及让 freezer 成为寻常厨房用词，最初指冰箱的冷冻室。

items.en: Today freezer covers both the standalone chest freezer and the freezer compartment inside a refrigerator.
items.cn: 如今 freezer 既指独立的卧式冰柜，也指冰箱内置的冷冻室。

note.en: Freezer belongs to the cold chain of words; keep it apart from fridge, which cools rather than freezes.
note.cn: freezer 属于一组「冷」词；注意与 fridge 区分——fridge 是冷藏而非冷冻。

entries.definition: comparative of fresh; only spelled somewhat near freezer, root is unrelated
entries.definitionCN: fresh 的比较级；只是拼写与 freezer 略近，词根无关

entries.definition: to freeze again, especially thawed food
entries.definitionCN: 重新冷冻，尤指解冻后的食物，与 freezer 同根

entries.definition: a refrigerator that keeps food cool but not frozen
entries.definitionCN: 冰箱，只冷藏不冷冻，与 freezer 相邻但分工不同

entries.definition: the formal word for a cooling appliance
entries.definitionCN: 冰箱的正式说法，与 freezer 相对的是冷藏功能

entries.definition: an older cabinet cooled with ice blocks
entries.definitionCN: 旧式用冰块降温的柜子，是 freezer 的前身概念

normalIntro.cn: 把这个词读成 freeze 加 er，词义便一目了然。

normal.en: freeze + -er: the machine that does the freezing.
normal.cn: freeze + -er：执行「冷冻」动作的机器。

normal.en: Same pattern as cleaner, cooker, printer: tool nouns from verbs.
normal.cn: 构词与 cleaner、cooker、printer 相同：动词加后缀成工具名词。

normal.en: Pair it with fridge: fridge cools, freezer freezes.
normal.cn: 与 fridge 配对记：fridge 冷藏，freezer 冷冻。

normal.en: frozen food lives in the freezer; the words rhyme in form and fact.
normal.cn: frozen food 存在 freezer 里；两个词形义互相印证。

normal.en: Family of cold words: freeze, frost, frozen, freezer.
normal.cn: 冷词家族：freeze、frost、frozen、freezer。

abstract.en: Picture white mist rolling out when you open the lid.
abstract.cn: 想象掀开柜盖时白雾滚滚涌出的画面。

abstract.en: Hear the low hum that never stops behind the kitchen door.
abstract.cn: 倾听厨房门后那从未停歇的低沉嗡鸣。

abstract.en: Feel a hard frozen bag straight from the deep cold.
abstract.cn: 感受从深寒中取出冻得梆硬的袋子。

examples.en: Label the date on every bag before it goes into the freezer.
examples.cn: 每袋食物放进冰柜前，先在袋上标好日期。

examples.en: The freezer iced over because the door never closed tightly.
examples.cn: 由于柜门一直关不严，冰柜里结满了冰。

examples.en: A power cut at night quietly thawed everything in the freezer.
examples.cn: 夜里停电，冰柜里的东西悄悄化冻了。

root: freezer 由动词 freeze（古英语 frēosan，结冰；可追溯至原始日耳曼语重构形式 *frezaną）加工具后缀 -er（表「做……的东西」）构成，字面义即「使之冷冻的器具」。同根词有 frozen、freezing、frost。

sensesIntro.cn: 核心的设备义向上扩展到工业冷库，旁转指柜中所存的冻品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a humming box of deep cold that turns food to ice
core.cn: 核心意象：一台低鸣的深寒箱子，把食物冻成冰

branches.en: the appliance itself in the kitchen
branches.cn: 厨房里的冷冻设备本体

definition_zh: 血统；世系；祖先的总称；家族出身；（生物）共同祖先关系
definition_en: the whole line of people from whom someone descends, the background this line gives them, or the shared origin of a group or species
core_image: 一条从先人延伸到自己脚下的血脉长线，重点在整条线，而不是线上某一个人
scene: 她做了基因检测，报告把她的血统追溯到东欧一座小村庄。 She takes a DNA test, and the report traces her ancestry back to a small village in eastern Europe.
sceneCN: 这里 ancestry 是「作为整体的血统世系」（第 1 个义项：把许多代先人看作一条完整血脉）；句意：她做了基因检测，报告把她的血统世系追溯到东欧的一座小村庄。场景要点：检测报告、染色体图、迁徙路线、小村庄的地图标记、手指点着报告上的一条线。

pos.zh: 血统；世系；祖先的总称；出身

derivatives.zh: 在祖先方面；按祖先的方式

senses.title: The whole line of descent
senses.definition: the complete line of people from whom a person or group is descended, considered as one whole
senses.definitionCN: 某个人或群体所出自的、被当作一个整体的完整先人链条
senses.example: Her ancestry reaches back to fishing families on the northern coast.
senses.exampleCN: 她的血统可以追溯到北方海岸的渔民家庭。
senses.why: -ry makes a collective noun: it gathers many ancestors into one line, so ancestry names the whole rather than any single forebear.
senses.whyCN: -ry 构成集合名词：它把许多祖先聚成一条线，因此 ancestry 命名的是整体，而不是某一位先人。

senses.title: Family background as identity
senses.definition: a person's social, national, or ethnic background as defined by their forebears
senses.definitionCN: 由先人决定的个人社会、民族或族群背景
senses.example: The novelist wrote about her mixed ancestry with humor.
senses.exampleCN: 这位小说家用幽默的笔调写自己混合的血统背景。
senses.why: Once the line is a possession, it becomes part of identity; ancestry then answers 'where do you come from?' rather than 'who was your great-grandfather?'
senses.whyCN: 一旦这条线成为一种拥有物，它就变成身份的一部分；ancestry 于是回答“你从哪里来”，而不是“你的曾祖父是谁”。

senses.title: The traceable genealogical record
senses.definition: the chain of descent that can be followed through documents, names, and records
senses.definitionCN: 可以通过文件、姓名和记录逐环追查的血统链
senses.example: He spent ten years tracing his ancestry through parish registers.
senses.exampleCN: 他花了十年时间通过教区登记簿追溯自己的世系。
senses.why: A line can be followed link by link; when the links are documented, ancestry becomes the traceable genealogy itself.
senses.whyCN: 一条线可以一环一环地追下去；当这些环节有文献记录时，ancestry 就变成可追溯的谱系本身。

senses.title: Evolutionary common origin
senses.definition: the earlier population or species from which a present organism is descended
senses.definitionCN: 现存生物所由来的早期种群或物种
senses.example: The two bird species share a common ancestry in the southern continent.
senses.exampleCN: 这两种鸟在南半球大陆上拥有共同祖先。
senses.why: Biology borrows the family tree and replaces named relatives with populations; shared ancestry is the branching point where two lines separate.
senses.whyCN: 生物学借用了家族树，把有名字的亲属换成种群；共同血统就是两条谱系分开的那个分叉点。

senses.title: Inherited genetic material
senses.definition: the inherited genetic material of an individual or population
senses.definitionCN: 某个人或群体所继承的遗传物质
senses.example: The clinic uses ancestry to check for inherited risk variants.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所利用血统信息检查遗传性风险变异。
senses.why: In modern genetics the abstract line is measured as DNA; ancestry becomes the sum of inherited variants, a testable property rather than a family story.
senses.whyCN: 在现代遗传学里，抽象的血统线被测量为 DNA；ancestry 成为所继承变异的集合，是一种可检测的属性，而不是家族故事。

senses.title: Descent as a legal qualification
senses.definition: the fact of descent from a place or people, used to establish rights, citizenship, or status
senses.definitionCN: 从某地或某民族传下的事实，用来确立权利、公民身份或地位
senses.example: Citizenship was granted on the basis of ancestry rather than birthplace.
senses.exampleCN: 公民身份依据血统而非出生地授予。
senses.why: Law needs a rule that can be checked; descent from a national line becomes a formal qualification, so ancestry turns into evidence of belonging.
senses.whyCN: 法律需要一条可核查的规则；从某国血统传下成为正式资格，ancestry 于是变成归属的证据。

senses.title: The source of a word, custom, or idea
senses.titleCN: 词语、习俗或观念的渊源
senses.definition: the origin or line of development of a word, custom, or idea
senses.definitionCN: 某个词语、习俗或观念的最初来源或发展线
senses.example: The ancestry of the proverb can be traced through three languages.
senses.exampleCN: 这句谚语的渊源可以穿过三种语言追溯出来。
senses.why: Anything that develops can be given a line of predecessors; ancestry then means 'the chain of earlier sources' rather than biological descent.
senses.whyCN: 任何会发展的事物都可以被安排一条前身线；ancestry 于是表示“更早来源的链条”，而不是生物血统。

senses.title: The pedigree of domesticated stock
senses.definition: the line of forebears of a domesticated animal or plant, especially as recorded by breeders
senses.definitionCN: 家养动物或植物的先代链条，尤指育种者记录下来的谱系
senses.example: The breeder keeps careful records of the herd's ancestry.
senses.exampleCN: 育种者仔细记录牛群的谱系。
senses.why: Selective breeding treats animals like families; the pedigree is literally an ancestry record, so the word applies to stock as well as people.
senses.whyCN: 选育把动物当作家族来对待；血统记录字面上就是 ancestry record，因此这个词也适用于家畜，而不只适用于人。
