senses.title: The ancestors taken together
senses.definition: the ancestors of a person taken together, especially when they are addressed as a body in ceremony or literature
senses.definitionCN: 把某人的祖先们聚在一起看待，尤指在仪式或文学中被作为一个整体称呼时
senses.example: The ceremony calls on the ancestry to witness the marriage.
senses.exampleCN: 仪式召唤祖先们来见证这场婚礼。
senses.why: The collective noun can be personified: the line stands in for the dead as a group, so ancestry is occasionally used where ancestor(s) would be concrete.
senses.whyCN: 这个集合名词可以被拟人化：整条线代表死者群体，因此 ancestry 偶尔会出现在本可以用具体 ancestor(s) 的地方。

intro.en: Ancestry is the collective and abstract noun beside ancestor, not a variant spelling of it. Old French ancesserie, built on ancestre with the suffix -erie, names the whole line or stock; English -ry keeps that collective force, and the spelling was later reshaped under the influence of ancestor. The base goes back to Latin antecessor 'fore-goer' (ante 'before' + cedere 'to go'). Ancient is a look-alike from ante + -anus, not from antiquus; descendant is from scandere 'to climb', not from cedere.
intro.cn: ancestry 是 ancestor 旁边的集合/抽象名词，不是它的拼写变体。古法语 ancesserie 在 ancestre 上加 -erie，指整条世系或整个血统；英语 -ry 保留这种集合义，后来拼写又受 ancestor 影响而调整。基础词可追溯到拉丁语 antecessor“先行者”（ante“前”+ cedere“走”）。ancient 是来自 ante + -anus 的形近词，并非来自 antiquus；descendant 来自 scandere“爬”，并非来自 cedere。

items.en: First recorded in English as auncestrie, 'series or line of ancestors, descent from ancestors'. The word names the line, not one person in it.
items.cn: 英语最早记录为 auncestrie，意为“祖先的序列或世系、从祖先传下”。这个词命名的是整条线，而不是线中的某个人。

items.en: From Old French ancesserie 'ancestry, ancestors, forefathers', formed on ancestre 'ancestor'. The French noun already had a collective sense.
items.cn: 来自古法语 ancesserie“血统、祖先、父辈”，由 ancestre“祖先”构成。这个法语名词本身已带集合义。

items.en: The French suffix -erie (English -ry) forms nouns of state, collection, or place. Added to ancestre it does not name one forebear but the whole stock or line; English later respelled the word under the influence of ancestor.
items.cn: 法语后缀 -erie（英语 -ry）构成状态、集合或地点名词。加在 ancestre 上，它不指某一位先人，而指整个血统或世系；英语后来受 ancestor 影响改写了拼写。

items.en: ancestre goes back to Late Latin antecessor 'predecessor', literally 'fore-goer', from antecedere 'to precede' = ante 'before' + cedere 'to go'.
items.cn: ancestre 可追溯到晚期拉丁语 antecessor“前任”，字面义“先行者”，来自 antecedere“走在前面”= ante“前”+ cedere“走”。

items.en: ante is traced to PIE *ant- 'front, forehead' and cedere to *ked- 'to go, yield'. The reconstructions are standard, but the exact route through Late Latin is not fully certain.
items.cn: ante 被追溯到原始印欧语 *ant-“前面、额头”，cedere 追溯到 *ked-“走、让步”。这些重构是通行的，但经过晚期拉丁语的具体路径并非完全确定。

items.en: Ancestry keeps the abstract or collective meaning, while ancestor is the countable person. It is not related to ancient as a derivative: ancient comes from ante + -anus, and antique is the word from antiquus. The opposite-direction cedere relative is successor, not descendant.
items.cn: ancestry 保留抽象或集合义，而 ancestor 是可数的人。它不是 ancient 的派生词：ancient 来自 ante + -anus，来自 antiquus 的是 antique。反向的 cedere 同根词是 successor，不是 descendant。

note.en: The first group separates the person noun, the adjective, and the look-alike from ancestry; the second compares words about lines, origins, and inheritance.
note.cn: 第一组把人物名词、形容词和形近词同 ancestry 分开；第二组比较关于世系、来源与继承的词。

entries.definition: one forebear. Ancestry is the whole line; ancestor is one countable link in it.
entries.definitionCN: 一位先人。ancestry 是整条线；ancestor 是线中一个可数的环节。

entries.definition: relating to ancestors. It describes a thing or place; ancestry is the noun for the line itself.
entries.definitionCN: 与祖先有关的。它描述某物或某地；ancestry 是表示这条线本身的名词。

entries.definition: belonging to the distant past. It shares the *ant- 'before' root but is not a form of ancestry, and it does not come from antiquus.
entries.definitionCN: 属于遥远过去的。它共享 *ant-“前”词根，但不是 ancestry 的形式，也不来自 antiquus。

entries.definition: a female ancestor. It is a derived person noun, not the collective line.
entries.definitionCN: 女祖先。它是派生的人物名词，不是集合性的世系。

entries.definition: a direct line of descent from an ancestor, especially a documented or formal one. It often stresses noble or official descent, while ancestry is broader and more personal.
entries.definitionCN: 从某位祖先传下的直系血统，尤指有记录或正式的血统。它常强调贵族或官方世系，而 ancestry 更宽泛、更个人化。

entries.definition: the fact of coming from a particular ancestor or group. It is the relation viewed from the descendant's side; ancestry is the total stock behind that relation.
entries.definitionCN: 出自某位祖先或某个群体的事实。它是从后代一方看的关系；ancestry 则是这一关系背后的全部血统储备。

entries.definition: the study or record of family lines. It is the research or chart, while ancestry is the biological or social fact being researched.
entries.definitionCN: 对家族世系的研究或记录。它指研究或谱表，而 ancestry 是被研究的生物或社会事实。

entries.definition: the traditions, language, and property inherited from a group. It includes culture and things, while ancestry is specifically the line of people.
entries.definitionCN: 从某个群体继承的传统、语言和财产。它包含文化与实物，而 ancestry 特指人的血统线。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: ancestor plus the French collective suffix -erie/-ry, the contrast with the countable ancestor, and the near words lineage, descent and genealogy.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：ancestor 加法语集合后缀 -erie/-ry，与可数 ancestor 的对比，以及 lineage、descent、genealogy 这组近义词。

normal.en: ancestry is ancestor + the French collective suffix -erie/-ry; the suffix gathers many ancestors into one line.
normal.cn: ancestry 是 ancestor 加法语集合后缀 -erie/-ry；这个后缀把许多祖先聚成一条线。

normal.en: Ancestor names one person; ancestry names the whole stock or line, so the two are not interchangeable.
normal.cn: ancestor 指一个人；ancestry 指整个血统或世系，两者不能互换。

normal.en: The spelling was reshaped by ancestor, which is why ancestry looks as if it contains the whole noun ancestor.
normal.cn: 拼写受 ancestor 影响而调整，所以 ancestry 看起来像把整个 ancestor 包了进去。

normal.en: Ancient is not the adjective of ancestry; the adjective is ancestral. Ancient comes from ante + -anus, while antique comes from antiquus.
normal.cn: ancient 不是 ancestry 的形容词；形容词是 ancestral。ancient 来自 ante + -anus，而 antique 来自 antiquus。

normal.en: Lineage stresses a documented line, descent the relation from the descendant's side, and genealogy the study or chart; ancestry is the broad fact behind all three.
normal.cn: lineage 强调有记录的世系，descent 强调从后代一方看的关系，genealogy 指研究或谱表；ancestry 是三者背后的宽泛事实。

abstract.en: Imagine a rope braided from many strands: each strand is an ancestor, the braided rope is ancestry.
abstract.cn: 想象一根由许多股编成的绳：每一股是一个 ancestor，编成的整根绳就是 ancestry。

abstract.en: A river delta: many upstream streams feed one channel; the streams are ancestors and their combined watershed is ancestry.
abstract.cn: 一片河口三角洲：上游许多溪流汇入一条水道；溪流是 ancestors，它们合起来的分水岭就是 ancestry。

abstract.en: A pedigree chart: one box is a person, but the connected chain of boxes is the ancestry.
abstract.cn: 一张谱系图：一个方框是一个人，而连起来的整串方框才是 ancestry。

examples.en: She discovered that her ancestry includes both farmers and sailors.
examples.cn: 她发现自己的血统里既有农民也有水手。

examples.en: Researchers use DNA to estimate shared ancestry among populations.
examples.cn: 研究人员用 DNA 估计群体间的共同血统。

examples.en: The law grants citizenship on the basis of ancestry.
examples.cn: 这项法律依据血统授予公民身份。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺家谱」——‘俺’家的谱系一代代传下来 → ancestry 血统、世系（只借音，不表词源）

root: 古法语 ancesserie < ancestre < 拉丁语 antecessor“先行者”（ante 前 + cedere 走）；-ry/-erie 使具体先人变成“血统总体、世系”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of ancestry all treat descent as a whole: the line itself, the identity it gives, its traceable record, a species' branching point, its DNA, a legal qualification, a cultural source, a pedigree, and the ancestors personified.
sensesIntro.cn: ancestry 的九个义项都把血统当作整体来处理：这条线本身、它带来的身份、可追溯的记录、物种的分叉点、它的 DNA、法律资格、文化渊源、谱系记录，以及被拟人化的祖先群体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the whole braided line of descent, seen as one thing rather than as separate people.
core.cn: 核心意象：一整条编合起来的血统线，被当作一个整体，而不是分开的许多人。

branches.en: THE LINE AS A WHOLE: the abstract descent, and the same ancestors personified as a body.
branches.cn: 作为整体的线：抽象的血统世系，以及被拟人化为群体的同一批祖先。

branches.en: IDENTITY AND STATUS: background becomes personal identity, and descent becomes a legal qualification.
branches.cn: 身份与地位：背景成为个人身份，血统成为法律资格。

branches.en: RECORDED LINES: parish registers trace a family, and breeders' records trace a pedigree.
branches.cn: 被记录的线：教区登记簿追溯家族，育种记录追溯谱系。

branches.en: BIOLOGY: populations share a branching origin, and modern genetics measures that origin as DNA.
branches.cn: 生物学：种群共享一个分叉来源，现代遗传学把这一来源测量为 DNA。

branches.en: CULTURAL SOURCE: words, customs and ideas can have a chain of earlier sources too.
branches.cn: 文化渊源：词语、习俗和观念也可以有一条更早来源的链条。

intro.en: Ancestry is ancestre + the French suffix -erie, continued in English as -ry. The suffix is the key: it changes a countable person noun into a collective or state noun. The base ancestre is the same word that gives ancestor, and it goes back to Latin antecessor.
intro.cn: ancestry 是 ancestre 加法语后缀 -erie，在英语中延续为 -ry。关键就在这个后缀：它把可数的人物名词变成集合或状态名词。基础词 ancestre 与 ancestor 同源，可追溯到拉丁语 antecessor。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is antecessor 'fore-goer' from antecedere (ante 'before' + cedere 'to go'). Cedere also gives predecessor and successor, but not descendant, which belongs to scandere 'to climb'. The deepest *ant- and *ked- roots are reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语基础是 antecessor“先行者”，来自 antecedere（ante“前”+ cedere“走”）。cedere 也构成 predecessor 和 successor，但不构成 descendant，后者属于 scandere“爬”。最深层的 *ant- 与 *ked- 词根是重构形式。

items.meaningCN: 血统；世系（-ry 构成集合或状态名词）
items.example: The census records are useful for studying ancestry.
items.exampleCN: 人口普查记录对研究血统很有用。

items.structure: ante- (before) + cedere (go), through Late Latin antecessor
items.meaning: one who goes before; a forebear
items.meaningCN: 先行者；祖先（ante- 前 + cedere 走）
items.example: Every ancestor in the chart has a birth record.
items.exampleCN: 谱系图中的每一位祖先都有出生记录。

items.meaningCN: 祖先的；与先人有关的（-al 构成关系形容词）
items.example: The ancestral house is now a small museum.
items.exampleCN: 那座祖宅现在是一座小博物馆。

items.example: The ancestress left a diary that covers forty years.
items.exampleCN: 这位女祖先留下了一本跨越四十年的日记。

items.meaning: in a way that relates to ancestors
items.meaningCN: 在祖先方面；按祖先的方式（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The family was ancestrally tied to the same valley.
items.exampleCN: 这个家族在血统上与同一座山谷相连。

items.meaningCN: 前事；先行者（ante- 前 + cedere 走 + -ent）
items.example: The custom has an antecedent in an older harvest rite.
items.exampleCN: 这一习俗的前身是一种更古老的丰收仪式。

items.meaning: someone or something that came before
items.meaningCN: 前任；前身（prae- 前 + de- 离 + cedere 走）
items.example: The predecessor of the archive was a private collection.
items.exampleCN: 这个档案馆的前身是一批私人收藏。

items.meaningCN: 继任者；后继者（sub- 后 + cedere 走）
items.example: The successor inherited the same record-keeping duty.
items.exampleCN: 继任者继承了他们同样的记录职责。

items.structure: de- (down) + scandere (climb); not a cedere word
items.meaning: a person or thing that comes from an earlier one
items.meaningCN: 后代；衍生物（de- 下 + scandere 爬；不是 cedere 同根词）
items.example: The descendants of the first settlers still live nearby.
items.exampleCN: 最早定居者的后代仍住在附近。

items.structure: Latin ante (before) + -anus, through Vulgar Latin *anteanus; not from antiquus
items.meaningCN: 古老的；古代的（ante 前 + -anus；并非来自 antiquus）
items.example: The ancient records were copied onto new paper.
items.exampleCN: 那些古老的记录被抄到了新纸上。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb; source of descend and descendant, not of ancestry
latinEntries.meaningCN: 爬；攀登（descend/descendant 的来源，不是 ancestry 的来源）

definition_zh: 美学；审美观；（事物给人的）美感、外观设计
definition_en: the branch of philosophy concerned with beauty and art, or the visual qualities and style of something
core_image: 一个人在看一件东西时先被它的样子打动，再追问自己为什么被打动
scene: 展厅里，观众先注意到墙面颜色与灯光，然后才读作品说明。 The new gallery's aesthetics put the visitor's eye before the label.
sceneCN: 这里 aesthetics 指「空间给人的整体视觉风格与美感」（第 3 个义项：某物的外观与视觉品质）；句意为这座新画廊的视觉设计让观众先看，再读标签。

pos.zh: 美学（学科，作单数）；审美观（可作复数意义）；外观美感

derivatives.zh: aesthetics 去掉 -s → 审美的；从「学科」回到「性质」
aesthetic + -ally（副词）→ 在审美上；从「性质」转到「评价方式」
aesthetic + -e（人）→ 审美者；从「感知」转到「以美为价值的人」
aesthetic + -ism（主义）→ 唯美主义；从「审美」转到「把美当作最高价值的主张」
an-（无）+ aisthēsis（感知）→ 麻醉；同根但语义相反：从「感知」转到「失去感知」

senses.title: The philosophy of beauty and art
senses.titleCN: 研究美与艺术的哲学分支
senses.definition: the branch of philosophy that studies beauty, art and taste
senses.definitionCN: 研究美、艺术与趣味的哲学分支
senses.example: Aesthetics asks what makes an object beautiful.
senses.exampleCN: 美学追问是什么让一件物品成为美的。
senses.why: The name was coined for a science of sensory knowledge; as philosophy took it up, the field narrowed to beauty, art and the judgement of taste.
senses.whyCN: 这个名称最初指关于感官知识的科学；哲学接管后，领域收窄到美、艺术与趣味判断。

senses.title: The study of sensory perception
senses.titleCN: 对感官感知的研究（原义）
senses.definition: the original sense: the study of perception through the senses
senses.definitionCN: 原初义：研究通过感官获得的感知
senses.example: Baumgarten founded aesthetics as the science of sensory perception.
senses.exampleCN: 鲍姆加登把美学建立为研究感官感知的科学。
senses.why: Greek aisthēsis is 'perception', so the first coinage named a theory of sensory experience before it named a theory of beauty.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 aisthēsis 是「感知」，因此最初的造词命名的是感官经验理论，而不是美的理论。

senses.title: The visual character of an object
senses.titleCN: 某物的外观与视觉品质
senses.definition: the visual qualities and overall look of a building, object or space
senses.definitionCN: 建筑、物件或空间的视觉品质与整体观感
senses.example: The new gallery's aesthetics put the visitor's eye before the label.
senses.exampleCN: 这座新画廊的视觉设计让观众先看，再读标签。
senses.why: From the study of perception the word slid to the perceived quality itself: what the eye meets can be called its aesthetics.
senses.whyCN: 从对感知的研究，词义滑向被感知的品质本身：眼睛所遇之物就可以被称为它的 aesthetics。

senses.title: The design principles of a movement
senses.titleCN: 某个流派或时代的设计原则
senses.definition: the set of visual principles associated with a movement or period
senses.definitionCN: 与某个流派或时期相关的一套视觉原则
senses.example: Modernist aesthetics favoured clean lines and exposed structure.
senses.exampleCN: 现代主义美学偏爱干净的线条与外露的结构。
senses.why: A movement is a shared way of seeing, so its principles can be summed up as an aesthetics: a doctrine of what looks right.
senses.whyCN: 流派是一种共享的观看方式，因此其原则可总括为一种 aesthetics：关于什么看起来正确的信条。

senses.title: A personal system of taste
senses.definition: a person's or group's set of preferences about beauty
senses.definitionCN: 个人或群体关于美的偏好集合
senses.example: His aesthetics are severe: no ornament, no colour.
senses.exampleCN: 他的审美很严厉：不要装饰，不要色彩。
senses.why: The discipline's name becomes countable in use: each person can hold a small theory of beauty, and that theory is called their aesthetics.
senses.whyCN: 学科名称在使用中变得可数：每个人都能持有一套关于美的小理论，这套理论就叫他的 aesthetics。

senses.title: Beauty as a selling point
senses.definition: the aesthetic appeal of a product, treated as a commercial quality
senses.definitionCN: 产品在审美上的吸引力，被当作商业品质
senses.example: The phone's aesthetics matter as much as its battery.
senses.exampleCN: 这部手机的外观美感与电池同样重要。
senses.why: Industry turned the word into a market attribute: a product is judged by how it looks, and that looks is its aesthetics.
senses.whyCN: 产业把这个词变成市场属性：产品按外观被评判，而外观就是它的 aesthetics。

senses.title: The look of a screen or game
senses.titleCN: 屏幕作品或游戏的视觉风格
senses.definition: the distinctive visual style of a film, game or interface
senses.definitionCN: 电影、游戏或界面的独特视觉风格
senses.example: The game's retro aesthetics borrow from early arcade cabinets.
senses.exampleCN: 这款游戏的复古视觉风格借鉴了早期街机框体。
senses.why: Digital media inherited the commercial sense and narrowed it to style: the whole look, not one beautiful object, is now the aesthetics.
senses.whyCN: 数字媒介继承了商业义并把它收窄为风格：整套外观，而不是单件美物，如今成了 aesthetics。

senses.title: Beauty in nature and environment
senses.definition: the aesthetic qualities of landscapes and environments, as a field of study
senses.definitionCN: 景观与环境的审美品质，作为研究领域
senses.example: Environmental aesthetics studies the beauty of coasts and forests.
senses.exampleCN: 环境美学研究海岸与森林之美。
senses.why: The discipline extended its questions from artworks to the natural world, so landscapes can have an aesthetics of their own.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科把问题从艺术品扩展到自然世界，因此景观也可以有自己的 aesthetics。

intro.en: Aesthetics was coined in modern philosophy from Greek aisthēsis 'perception' and entered English around 1800 through German and French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: aesthetics 由近代哲学用希腊 aisthēsis「感知」造成，约 1800 年经德语与法语进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Aisthēsis meant 'perception by the senses'; the verb aisthanesthai meant 'to perceive, feel'.
items.cn: aisthēsis 意为「通过感官的感知」；动词 aisthanesthai 意为「感知、感受」。

items.en: Aisthētikos meant 'of or for sense perception, perceptible'; it supplied the adjective behind the modern noun.
items.cn: aisthētikos 意为「与感官感知有关的、可感知的」，为现代名词提供了形容词基础。

items.en: Alexander Baumgarten coined Ästhetik in the eighteenth century for the science of sensuous knowledge; Kant used the term for the conditions of perception.
items.cn: 亚历山大·鲍姆加登于 18 世纪造出 Ästhetik，指关于感官知识的科学；康德用这个词指感知的条件。

items.en: English aesthetic is recorded from 1798 and aesthetics from 1803, both from German or French models.
items.cn: 英语 aesthetic 自 1798 年有记录，aesthetics 自 1803 年有记录，均来自德语或法语模板。

items.en: In the nineteenth century the term moved from sensory perception to the criticism of taste, and beauty became its central question.
items.cn: 到 19 世纪，这个词从感官感知转到趣味批评，美成为其核心问题。

items.en: Reconstructed form: the deeper root of aisthanesthai is given as PIE *au- 'to perceive', a reconstruction with no surviving written witness.
items.cn: 重构形式：aisthanesthai 的更早词根被拟为印欧 *au-「感知」，这一重构没有留存的书面证据。

note.en: Group one holds the aisth- family, including a medical word that looks like its opposite; group two holds neighbouring ways of talking about beauty and style.
note.cn: 第一组是 aisth- 词族，其中还包括一个看似反义的医学词；第二组是谈论美与风格的邻近说法。

entries.definition: The adjective 'concerning beauty', or a noun for one principle of taste; aesthetics is the field or the overall look.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词「关于美的」，或名词指一条审美原则；aesthetics 是学科或整体观感。

entries.definition: A person devoted to beauty and refined taste; the word often suggests cultivated sensibility.
entries.definitionCN: 献身于美与精致品味的人；常暗示有教养的感受力。

entries.definition: The belief that beauty should be valued for itself, especially the art-for-art's-sake movement.
entries.definitionCN: 认为美应因其自身而被珍视的主张，尤指「为艺术而艺术」运动。

entries.definition: Loss of sensation, especially under medical anaesthetic; an- 'without' plus aisthēsis 'perception' makes it the exact negative of the root.
entries.definitionCN: 感觉丧失，尤指麻醉状态；an-「无」加 aisthēsis「感知」，使它正好是这个词根的反义。

entries.definition: The philosophical study of art, including questions of meaning and ontology; aesthetics is its older and often narrower name.
entries.definitionCN: 对艺术的哲学研究，包括意义与存在问题；aesthetics 是更古老、通常也更窄的名称。

entries.definition: The practice of evaluating particular works; it applies aesthetic ideas but is not the theory itself.
entries.definitionCN: 评价具体作品的实践；会应用美学观念，但本身不是理论。

entries.definition: The ability to discern what is good or beautiful; aesthetics studies taste, while taste is the capacity being studied.
entries.definitionCN: 辨别何为好或美的能力；美学研究趣味，而趣味是被研究的能力。

entries.definition: A characteristic way of making or appearing; aesthetics is the broader inquiry into why a style pleases.
entries.definitionCN: 制作或呈现的独特方式；aesthetics 是追问一种风格为何令人愉悦的更广研究。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real compounds and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek aisthēsis 'perception' + -ics 'the study of': the study of what the senses take in.
normal.cn: 希腊 aisthēsis「感知」+ -ics「……学」：研究感官接收到的东西。

normal.en: Baumgarten coined the German term in the eighteenth century for sensory knowledge, not for beauty alone.
normal.cn: 鲍姆加登在 18 世纪造出德语术语，指感官知识，而不只是美。

normal.en: The pair aesthetic and anesthesia share the root: one turns perception on, the other off.
normal.cn: aesthetic 与 anesthesia 共享词根：一个打开感知，一个关闭感知。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the modern uses: visual aesthetics, the aesthetics of a building, environmental aesthetics.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显出今用：视觉美学、建筑外观、环境美学。

normal.en: The family runs aesthetic, aesthetics, aesthete, aestheticism and aesthetically.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 aesthetic、aesthetics、aesthete、aestheticism 与 aesthetically。

abstract.en: Picture an eye that feels first and asks questions afterwards.
abstract.cn: 想象一只先感受、后提问的眼睛。

abstract.en: Picture a room whose colours seem to decide how you stand in it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个房间，颜色似乎决定了你站立的方式。

abstract.en: Picture a switch that can turn feeling off, which is what anesthesia does.
abstract.cn: 想象一个能把感觉关掉的开关，麻醉做的正是这件事。

examples.en: Aesthetics and ethics are separate questions, though artists often mix them.
examples.cn: 美学与伦理是两个问题，尽管艺术家常把它们混在一起。

examples.en: The car was redesigned for aesthetics rather than for luggage space.
examples.cn: 这款车重新设计是为了外观美感，而不是行李空间。

examples.en: She wrote on the aesthetics of everyday objects rather than on painting.
examples.cn: 她写的是日常物品的审美，而不是绘画。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「aes（近似「爱死」）+ thetics」——爱到极致的感受 → 美学

root: 希腊 aisthēsis「感知」、aisthētikos「可感知的」；鲍姆加登 18 世纪以 Ästhetik 指感官知识之学，英语 aesthetic 1798 年、aesthetics 1803 年。更早词根拟为印欧 *au-「感知」，属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the philosophy of beauty back to its original study of perception, then out to the look of objects, movements, products, screens and landscapes.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从美的哲学出发，回到最初的感知研究，再向外扩展到物件、流派、产品、屏幕与景观的外观。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person is first moved by how something looks, then asks why it moved them.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人先被某物的样子打动，再追问自己为什么被打动。

branches.en: THE STUDY AND ITS ROOT: beauty as a philosophical question, then perception as the older subject.
branches.cn: 学科及其根：美作为哲学问题，然后是更早的感知主题。

branches.en: WHAT THE EYE MEETS: an object's look, and the look of a whole landscape.
branches.cn: 眼睛所遇：一件物件的外观，以及整片景观的外观。

branches.en: SHARED PRINCIPLES: a movement turns private taste into a doctrine of form.
branches.cn: 共享原则：流派把私人趣味变成关于形式的信条。

branches.en: PRIVATE TASTE: each person carries a small theory of what looks right.
branches.cn: 私人趣味：每个人都带着一套关于「什么看起来对」的小理论。

branches.en: SOLD AND SCREENED: appearance becomes a product feature and then a whole digital style.
branches.cn: 被售卖与被投影：外观先成为产品卖点，再成为整套数字风格。

intro.en: Aesthetics is a Greek root plus a Greek-derived suffix of study; the same root builds the adjective, the person and the medical negative.
intro.cn: aesthetics 是希腊词根加希腊来源的「学问」后缀；同一词根还构成形容词、指人的名词与医学上的反义词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor here: the word is Greek aisthēsis plus -ics, and Latin only transmitted Greek philosophy into modern languages.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁祖先：词由希腊 aisthēsis 加 -ics 构成，拉丁语只把希腊哲学传给了现代语言。

items.example: The root concerns feeling, not beauty as such.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根关心的是感受，而不是美本身。

items.meaning: a field of study or practice
items.example: Physics and ethics use the same ending.
items.exampleCN: physics 与 ethics 用的是同一个词尾。

items.example: The noun supplies the stem of the modern term.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供现代术语的词干。

items.meaning: the study of perception, later of beauty
items.example: Aesthetics became a university subject.
items.exampleCN: 美学成为一门大学学科。

items.example: The aesthetic judgement came before the price.
items.exampleCN: 审美判断先于价格出现。

items.example: The bridge is aesthetically successful.
items.exampleCN: 这座桥在审美上是成功的。

items.example: The aesthete refused to own an ugly chair.
items.exampleCN: 这位审美者拒绝拥有一把难看的椅子。

items.meaning: devotion to beauty for its own sake
items.example: Aestheticism shaped the decade's interiors.
items.exampleCN: 唯美主义塑造了那个年代的室内风格。

items.example: The drug produces anesthesia.
items.exampleCN: 这种药使人失去感觉。

definition_zh: 贸易顺差；贸易盈余；出口大于进口的差额
definition_en: the amount by which a country's exports of goods exceed its imports in a given period
core_image: 一架天平，出口一侧的砝码堆得更高，进口一侧翘起，秤杆上标出一个正数
scene: 经济部门的简报会上，分析员把全年出口额与进口额相减，得出一个可以让公众安心的正差额。 The report showed a trade surplus for the second year running.
sceneCN: 这里指「出口超过进口的差额」，对应第 1 个义项：一定时期内出口总值大于进口总值的部分；句意为报告显示该国连续第二年出现贸易顺差。画面要点：简报屏幕、两条柱状数据、天平、正号标记。

pos.zh: 贸易顺差；贸易盈余（可数，复数 trade surpluses）

derivatives.zh: 盈余；过剩的（短语的核心名词，指多出的部分）
多余部分（surplus 加表示集合的名词后缀，法律用语，指剩余之物）
多笔盈余（surplus 加复数后缀，语义由单笔转为多笔）
贸易；交易（短语的前半，源自古英语与低地德语中表示「路径、往来」的词）
交易活动（trade 加动名词后缀，指持续的买卖）

senses.title: Exports exceeding imports
senses.definition: the amount by which the value of a country's exports exceeds the value of its imports in a period
senses.definitionCN: 一定时期内一国出口总值超过进口总值的部分
senses.example: The report showed a trade surplus for the second year running.
senses.exampleCN: 报告显示该国连续第二年出现贸易顺差。
senses.why: Latin superplus means 'something more over', so the phrase names the value left over after goods going out outweigh goods coming in.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 superplus 意为「多在上面的东西」，因此这个短语指出去多于进来之后剩下的那部分价值。

senses.title: The size of the gap
senses.definition: the measured amount of the excess, usually in money terms
senses.definitionCN: 这一超出部分的计量规模，通常以货币计
senses.example: The trade surplus reached sixty billion dollars.
senses.exampleCN: 贸易顺差达到六百亿美元。
senses.why: Surplus is countable, so the phrase names a figure that grows, shrinks or sets a record.
senses.whyCN: surplus 可数，因此这个短语指一个会增长、收缩或创纪录的数字。

senses.title: A bilateral surplus with one partner
senses.titleCN: 与某一贸易伙伴的双边顺差
senses.definition: the excess of exports to one country over imports from that country
senses.definitionCN: 向某一国出口超过从该国进口的部分
senses.example: The trade surplus with that partner drew complaints.
senses.exampleCN: 与那个伙伴的贸易顺差引发了抱怨。
senses.why: Trade is tracked partner by partner, so the excess can be assigned to a single relationship.
senses.whyCN: 贸易按伙伴逐一对计，因此这份超出可归属于单一关系。

senses.title: The surplus in goods alone
senses.definition: the excess measured on goods only, leaving services aside
senses.definitionCN: 只按货物计算、把服务放在一边的超出部分
senses.example: The goods trade surplus offsets the services deficit.
senses.exampleCN: 货物贸易顺差抵消了服务逆差。
senses.why: Statistical ledgers separate goods and services, so the phrase is often qualified to show which one is meant.
senses.whyCN: 统计账目把货物与服务分开，因此这个短语常被限定，以说明看的是哪一本账。

senses.title: The surplus as a share of the economy
senses.titleCN: 以占经济总量的比例表示的顺差
senses.definition: the surplus expressed as a percentage of gross domestic product
senses.definitionCN: 以国内生产总值的百分比表示的顺差
senses.example: The trade surplus equals five percent of output.
senses.exampleCN: 贸易顺差相当于产出的百分之五。
senses.why: A raw number needs scale, so economists divide the excess by the size of the economy.
senses.whyCN: 裸数字需要尺度，因此经济学家用经济规模来除这份超出。

senses.title: The surplus and where it goes
senses.definition: the surplus viewed together with the reserves or capital exports it funds
senses.definitionCN: 与由其形成的外汇储备或资本输出一并看待的顺差
senses.example: The trade surplus was recycled into foreign bonds.
senses.exampleCN: 贸易顺差被转化为对外债券投资。
senses.why: Money earned abroad must be held or lent somewhere, so a surplus always has a financial destination.
senses.whyCN: 在海外赚到的钱总得存放或借出，因此顺差总有一个金融去向。

senses.title: The surplus as a political argument
senses.definition: the surplus used in debate as evidence of competitiveness or of unfair advantage
senses.definitionCN: 在争论中被用作竞争力或不公平优势之证据的顺差
senses.example: Officials cite the trade surplus when defending industrial policy.
senses.exampleCN: 官员在为产业政策辩护时援引贸易顺差。
senses.why: A single number is easy to campaign with, so the phrase gained a rhetorical life beyond accounting.
senses.whyCN: 一个数字便于宣传，因此这个短语获得了超出会计范围的说服力。

senses.title: The surplus shrinking or widening
senses.titleCN: 顺差的收缩或扩大趋势
senses.definition: the direction in which the excess is moving over successive periods
senses.definitionCN: 这份超出在连续各期中的变化方向
senses.example: Rising imports caused the trade surplus to shrink.
senses.exampleCN: 进口上升使贸易顺差收窄。
senses.why: Because the phrase names a flow over time, it is naturally described as widening, shrinking or disappearing.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个短语指一段时间内的流量，自然会有扩大、收窄或消失等说法。

intro.en: Trade surplus joins trade, a word of path and exchange, with surplus, from Latin superplus 'something more over'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: trade surplus 把表示「路径与往来」的 trade，与出自拉丁 superplus「多在上面的东西」的 surplus 组合起来。年代均为约数。

items.en: Trade probably entered English from Middle Low German or Dutch, where it meant a track or course, before English widened it to commerce.
items.cn: trade 很可能经中古低地德语或荷兰语进入英语，原指路径或行程，后来英语把它扩展到商业。

items.en: Super meant 'above, over', and it built many words about excess and position.
items.cn: super 意为「在上、超过」，构成许多表示超出与位置关系的词。

items.en: Plus meant 'more', and the combination superplus named what is left over above the need.
items.cn: plus 意为「更多」，组合成的 superplus 指超出所需而余下的部分。

items.en: Old French surplus carried the word into English in the fifteenth century as an amount left over.
items.cn: 古法语 surplus 在 15 世纪把这个词带入英语，指剩余之量。

items.en: Once trade statistics became routine, trade surplus was fixed as the positive counterpart of trade deficit.
items.cn: 贸易统计常规化之后，trade surplus 固定为 trade deficit 的正向对应说法。

note.en: The first group shares the excess root or looks close to it; the second group names related surpluses measured differently.
note.cn: 第一组共享「超出」词根或与之外形相近；第二组是算法不同的相关盈余。

entries.definition: Any amount left over; alone it may mean a budget surplus or unsold stock, while trade surplus specifies the goods account.
entries.definitionCN: 任何剩余之量；单独使用时可能指预算盈余或滞销存货，而 trade surplus 特指货物账目。

entries.definition: An unnecessary or extra part, used in legal drafting; it is about wording or property, not trade.
entries.definitionCN: 多余或额外的部分，用于法律起草；它关乎措辞或财产，不是贸易。

entries.definition: More than is needed; it describes redundancy, while a trade surplus is a measured balance.
entries.definitionCN: 超出所需；它描述冗余，而贸易顺差是一个被计量的差额。

entries.definition: Imports exceeding exports; the same ledger with the sign reversed.
entries.definitionCN: 进口超过出口；同一本账，符号相反。

entries.definition: A neutral word for the difference between exports and imports, without saying which side is larger.
entries.definitionCN: 出口与进口差额的中性说法，不说哪一侧更大。

entries.definition: An excess covering goods, services and income flows; a trade surplus is only the goods part.
entries.definitionCN: 涵盖货物、服务与收入流的超出；贸易顺差只是其中的货物部分。

entries.definition: A balance where credits exceed debits; it is the accounting description of what a surplus is.
entries.definitionCN: 贷方超过借方的余额；它是盈余在会计上的描述。

entries.definition: An amount beyond what is needed or expected; it lacks the trade and accounting precision of surplus.
entries.definitionCN: 超出所需或所期的量；它没有 surplus 那样的贸易与会计精度。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin excess words, the real trade word and real statistical phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁「超出」词、真实的贸易词与真实统计搭配。

normal.en: Super means over and plus means more, so surplus is what is left over and above.
normal.cn: super 意为在上，plus 意为更多，surplus 就是多出来、剩下来的部分。

normal.en: The opposite phrase is trade deficit, the same ledger with the other sign.
normal.cn: 反义说法是 trade deficit，同一本账的另一符号。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the uses: run a surplus, shrink the surplus, a record surplus.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示用法：出现顺差、缩小顺差、创纪录顺差。

normal.en: Surplus is countable, so it takes a, grows, shrinks and reaches a figure.
normal.cn: surplus 可数，因此能带冠词，能增长、收缩、达到某个数字。

normal.en: Keep the ledgers apart: goods, current account and government budget.
normal.cn: 要把几本账分开：货物账、经常账户账与政府预算账。

abstract.en: Picture a scale where the export pan sinks and the import pan rises, and a plus sign hangs on the beam.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平，出口那端下沉，进口那端翘起，横梁上挂着一个正号。

abstract.en: Picture a warehouse that ships out more than it receives, so the shelves slowly empty.
abstract.cn: 想象一座仓库，运出的比收进的多，架子慢慢变空。

abstract.en: Picture a country storing what it earned abroad in a vault it cannot easily spend at home.
abstract.cn: 想象一个国家把海外赚到的钱存在一座金库，而在国内却不容易花出去。

examples.en: The country has run a trade surplus for a decade.
examples.cn: 这个国家已连续十年保持贸易顺差。

examples.en: A large trade surplus pushed the currency upward.
examples.cn: 巨额贸易顺差推高了本国货币。

examples.en: Higher fuel imports erased the trade surplus.
examples.cn: 燃料进口增加抹去了贸易顺差。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「出口多、进口少，账上多一块」——surplus 是「多」，trade 是贸易 → 贸易顺差

root: trade 源自古英语与中古低地德语中表示「路径、往来」的词；surplus 出自拉丁 superplus「多在上面的东西」，由 super「在上」与 plus「更多」构成。合指出口大于进口的差额。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe one excess: exports over imports, its size, its bilateral form, its goods-only measure, its share of output, its destination, its political use and its direction over time.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项描述同一份超出：出口多于进口的部分、其数额、其双边形式、仅计货物的算法、其占产出的比例、其去向、其政治用途，以及其随时间的走向。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scale with the export pan heavier and a plus sign on the beam.
core.cn: 核心意象：一架天平，出口那端更重，横梁上有个正号。

branches.en: BASE EXCESS: the ledger records more outgoing than incoming value.
branches.cn: 基础超出：账上记的流出价值多于流入价值。

branches.en: MEASURE AND TREND: the excess has a size and a direction.
branches.cn: 数额与趋势：这份超出有大小，也有走向。

branches.en: ONE PARTNER: the excess can be assigned to a single relationship.
branches.cn: 单一伙伴：这份超出可归属于一段双边关系。

branches.en: SCOPE AND SCALE: goods alone, or the excess as a share of output.
branches.cn: 范围与尺度：或只计货物，或折算为产出的比例。

branches.en: MONEY AND POLITICS: the excess is parked abroad and argued over at home.
branches.cn: 金钱与政治：这份超出被存放在海外，也在国内被争论。

intro.en: Trade surplus is a phrase of two free words, one about exchange and one built from two Latin comparatives.
intro.cn: trade surplus 由两个自由词构成，一个讲往来，一个由两个拉丁比较级成分构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin super 'above' and plus 'more' give surplus, superfluous and superplus; trade has a Germanic origin and gives trading, trader and trademark.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 super「在上」与 plus「更多」衍生 surplus、superfluous 与 superplus；trade 源自日耳曼语，衍生 trading、trader 与 trademark。

items.example: The prefix marks what lies over a limit.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出超出界限之物。

items.example: The element adds quantity.
items.exampleCN: 这个成分表示增加的数量。

items.example: The surplus was sold off.
items.exampleCN: 剩余物资被卖掉。

items.example: The clause was surplusage.
items.exampleCN: 这一条款纯属多余。

items.example: The extra detail was superfluous.
items.exampleCN: 那处额外细节是多余的。

items.example: Trade linked the two ports.
items.exampleCN: 贸易把两个港口连在一起。

items.meaning: the activity of buying and selling
items.example: Trading opened at nine.
items.exampleCN: 九点开始交易。

items.example: A trader took the offer.
items.exampleCN: 一位交易者接受了报价。

items.example: The deficit widened.
items.exampleCN: 赤字扩大了。

items.example: They ran a trade surplus.
items.exampleCN: 他们出现了贸易顺差。

definition_zh: 统计的；统计学的；以统计数据为依据的
definition_en: relating to statistics, or based on numerical data gathered from many cases rather than on single examples
core_image: 一张巨大的表格被折成柱状图，成百上千的个人点数收拢成几根高低不同的柱子
scene: 这里指「统计的」。 The report offered statistical evidence that the policy had cut waiting times.
sceneCN: 这里 statistical 是「统计的、以数据为依据的」（第 2 个义项：用汇总数字而非个案来说明问题）；句意：报告给出了政策缩短等待时间的统计证据。图中可辨识物件：表格、柱状图、样本点、误差线。

pos.zh: 统计的；统计学的；以统计数据为依据的

senses.title: Belonging to the discipline of statistics
senses.definition: relating to statistics as a branch of mathematics that collects, summarizes and analyses data
senses.definitionCN: 与作为数学分支的统计学有关，该学科收集、汇总并分析数据
senses.example: Her statistical training let her detect a flaw in the sampling design.
senses.exampleCN: 她的统计学训练使她发现了抽样设计中的缺陷。
senses.why: The adjective simply marks membership in the field: anything taught in a statistics course, from distributions to estimators, can be called statistical.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是标记「属于该领域」：统计学课程里讲授的内容，从分布到估计量，都可以称为 statistical。

senses.title: Based on aggregated numbers
senses.definition: resting on numbers collected from many cases and summarized, rather than on one person's experience
senses.definitionCN: 建立在从许多案例收集并汇总的数字之上，而不是依据某个人的经历
senses.example: Statistical evidence linked seat-belt laws to fewer road deaths.
senses.exampleCN: 统计数据把安全带立法与道路死亡人数下降联系起来。
senses.why: Statistics began as the science of the state's numbers; the adjective therefore signals evidence at the level of a population, where individual stories become counts.
senses.whyCN: statistics 最初是研究「国家数据」的学问，因此这个形容词标示的是人口层面的证据，个人的故事在这里变成计数。

senses.title: Unlikely to be due to chance
senses.titleCN: 达到统计显著性：不太可能出于偶然
senses.definition: of a result, large enough relative to random variation that it is unlikely to have arisen by chance alone
senses.definitionCN: 指结果相对于随机波动足够大，单靠偶然出现的可能性很低
senses.example: The difference was statistical at the five percent level.
senses.exampleCN: 这一差异在百分之五的水平上具有统计显著性。
senses.why: Statisticians compare an observed difference with the spread that chance would produce; when the gap is large against that spread, the result earns the label statistical in this evaluative sense.
senses.whyCN: 统计学家把观察到的差异与偶然会造成的变化幅度相比较；当差距相对于该幅度足够大时，结果就在这种评价意义上获得 statistical 的标签。

senses.title: Estimating from a sample
senses.definition: of inference or probability, concerned with drawing conclusions about a whole from a limited sample
senses.definitionCN: 指推断或概率，关注如何从有限样本对整个总体得出结论
senses.example: Statistical inference turned the survey of two thousand voters into a forecast.
senses.exampleCN: 统计推断把两千名选民调查变成了预测。
senses.why: Because we rarely measure everyone, statistical reasoning works by assigning probabilities to claims about the unmeasured remainder; the adjective names that bridge from part to whole.
senses.whyCN: 因为我们很少能测量所有人，统计推理就通过给关于未测部分的判断分配概率来工作；这个形容词命名的正是「由部分到整体」的桥梁。

senses.title: Averaged over countless particles
senses.titleCN: 物理学中的统计方法：对大量粒子取平均
senses.definition: of mechanics or thermodynamics, describing the behaviour of a system through averages over very many particles rather than through each one
senses.definitionCN: 指力学或热力学，通过大量粒子的平均行为而不是逐个粒子来描述系统
senses.example: Statistical mechanics explains why a gas fills its container.
senses.exampleCN: 统计力学解释了气体为何会充满容器。
senses.why: Physics borrowed the word because tracking every molecule is impossible; temperature and pressure are statistical facts, meaningful only as averages.
senses.whyCN: 物理学借用这个词，因为追踪每一个分子是不可能的；温度与压强都是统计性事实，只有作为平均值才有意义。

senses.title: The group being measured
senses.definition: of a population or sample, referring to the complete set or the subset from which data are drawn
senses.definitionCN: 指总体或样本，即数据所取自的完整集合或其中的子集
senses.example: The statistical population included every adult in the county.
senses.exampleCN: 统计总体包括该县每一位成年人。
senses.why: Before any number can be computed, the statistician must define the group; the adjective marks that group as the object of measurement rather than as everyday 'people'.
senses.whyCN: 在计算任何数字之前，统计学家必须先界定群体；这个形容词把该群体标记为测量对象，而不是日常意义上的「人们」。

senses.title: Random variation, not a mistake
senses.titleCN: 统计误差：随机波动，而非操作错误
senses.definition: of error, the unavoidable scatter produced by sampling and randomness, as opposed to a blunder in measurement
senses.definitionCN: 指误差，即抽样与随机性造成的不可避免的离散，而不是测量中的操作失误
senses.example: Statistical error in the poll was plus or minus three points.
senses.exampleCN: 民调的统计误差为正负三个百分点。
senses.why: This sense corrects a common confusion: statistical error is a property of the method, whereas a mistake is a failure of the person, so the adjective separates noise from fault.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项纠正常见混淆：统计误差是方法本身的属性，而错误是人的失误；形容词由此把「噪声」与「过错」区分开。

senses.title: Odds attached to one case
senses.definition: describing the probability that a particular person or event falls into a risk category, as calculated from group data
senses.definitionCN: 指依据群体数据计算出的、某个具体人或事件落入某一风险类别的概率
senses.example: Insurers price policies by the statistical risk of each age group.
senses.exampleCN: 保险公司按各年龄组的统计风险为保单定价。
senses.why: Group data can be applied back to individuals as odds; this sense is where statistical language enters insurance, medicine and everyday risk talk.
senses.whyCN: 群体数据可以被反过来作为概率用于个人；正是在这一义项上，统计语言进入保险、医学与日常的风险讨论。

intro.en: Statistical is the adjective of statistics, a word coined in eighteenth-century German academia from New Latin statisticum and Latin status 'state, condition'. The adjective marks 'of state data' before it marks 'of mathematical methods'.
intro.cn: statistical 是 statistics 的形容词；statistics 由十八世纪德国学界用新拉丁 statisticum 与拉丁 status「国家、状态」造出。这个形容词先表示「关于国家数据的」，后表示「关于数学方法的」。

items.en: Latin status meant 'condition, position, state', from stare 'to stand'. It supplied the word for the commonwealth, the state, and also for the standing of affairs that officials wished to count.
items.cn: 拉丁 status 意为「状况、地位、国家」，出自 stare「站立」。它既提供「国家」一词，也指官员想要统计的「事务状况」。

items.en: In seventeenth- and eighteenth-century German universities, statisticum collegium named a course on the affairs of the state, gathering facts about population, trade and territory.
items.cn: 在十七、十八世纪的德国大学里，statisticum collegium 指讲授国家事务的课程，收集人口、贸易与领土方面的事实。

items.en: Achenwall's lectures of 1749 fixed Statistik as the name of this descriptive science of state facts, which is generally credited with launching the modern word.
items.cn: 阿亨瓦尔 1749 年的讲座把 Statistik 固定为这门描述国家事实的学问之名，一般认为现代这个词由此发端。

items.en: English adopted statistics in the late eighteenth century, at first for state facts and only later for the mathematical treatment of numerical data.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪末借入 statistics，最初指国家事实，后来才指对数值数据的数学处理。

items.en: The adjective statistical was formed on statistics and broadened in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries to cover probability, sampling and physics.
items.cn: 形容词 statistical 由 statistics 构成，并在十九、二十世纪扩展到概率、抽样与物理学。

items.en: The exact first English citation of statistical is uncertain. The Latin root status is clear, but the deeper Indo-European form *sta- is a reconstruction rather than a recorded word.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：statistical 的英语最早书证年代不确定。拉丁词根 status 清楚，但更深的印欧语形式 *sta- 是重构形式，并非有记录的真实词形。

note.en: The first group separates the statistics family by part of speech; the second gives near-synonyms for data-based reasoning.
note.cn: 第一组按词性区分 statistics 词族；第二组给出表示「以数据为依据」的近义词。

entries.definition: The discipline, or the body of data. Statistical is the adjective describing what belongs to it.
entries.definitionCN: 指学科或数据整体；statistical 是描述「属于它」的形容词。

entries.definition: One computed value such as a mean. The singular is countable; statistics as a subject is not.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个计算出来的数值，如平均数；单数可数，而作为学科的 statistics 不可数。

entries.definition: The person who analyses data. The adjective statistical describes the work, not the worker.
entries.definitionCN: 指分析数据的人；形容词 statistical 描述工作，而非工作者。

entries.definition: The adverb answering 'in what terms?' or 'by what measure?'. Statistical modifies a noun; statistically modifies a verb or adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，回答「从什么角度」「用什么度量」；statistical 修饰名词，statistically 修饰动词或形容词。

entries.definition: Given in numbers rather than words. It does not imply that the numbers were sampled or tested.
entries.definitionCN: 指用数字而非文字表达，并不隐含这些数字经过抽样或检验。

entries.definition: Concerned with quantities rather than qualities. It is broader than statistical, which specifically involves inference from data.
entries.definitionCN: 指关注数量而非性质，比 statistical 更宽泛，后者具体涉及由数据作出推断。

entries.definition: Expressed as a likelihood. Statistical results are often probabilistic, but probabilistic models need not use measured samples.
entries.definitionCN: 指以可能性来表达；统计结果常是概率性的，但概率模型并不一定使用实测样本。

entries.definition: Relating to the risk tables of insurers. It is a specialised application of statistical method to life and property risk.
entries.definitionCN: 指与保险公司的风险表有关，是统计方法在人身与财产风险上的专门应用。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: statistics + -al: of the discipline that turns cases into counts.
normal.cn: statistics + -al：属于那门把个案变成计数的学科。

normal.en: The family runs statistic, statistics, statistician, statistically, biostatistics.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 statistic、statistics、statistician、statistically、biostatistics。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the range: statistical analysis, statistical significance, statistical inference, statistical error.
normal.cn: 固定搭配展示范围：统计分析、统计显著性、统计推断、统计误差。

normal.en: A single case is an anecdote; a thousand cases become a statistic, and the method becomes statistical.
normal.cn: 一个个案是轶事，上千个个案成为统计量，方法也就成为 statistical。

normal.en: Statistical error is noise, not a blunder; keep the two apart.
normal.cn: 统计误差是噪声而不是失误，要把两者分开。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd of faces collapsing into a few coloured bars.
abstract.cn: 想象一群面孔收拢成几根彩色柱子。

abstract.en: Picture a net thrown over a river: it catches a sample, not the whole river.
abstract.cn: 想象一张网撒向河流：它捕到的是样本，不是整条河。

abstract.en: Picture a bell-shaped hill with two small tails marked 'unlikely'.
abstract.cn: 想象一座钟形山丘，两端各有一条标着「不太可能」的小尾巴。

examples.en: The paper's statistical analysis controlled for age and income.
examples.cn: 这篇论文的统计分析对年龄与收入作了控制。

examples.en: No statistical method can rescue a badly designed sample.
examples.cn: 再好的统计方法也救不了一个设计糟糕的样本。

examples.en: Statistical mechanics treats heat as the average motion of huge numbers of molecules.
examples.cn: 统计力学把热视为大量分子运动的平均值。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「statistics（统计）+ al」——看汇总数字而不是看个人 → statistical 统计的

root: 拉丁 status「国家、状态」（出自 stare「站立」）→ 新拉丁 statisticum「国家事务讲座」→ 德语 Statistik → 英语 statistics + -al。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses range from the discipline itself to aggregated evidence, significance testing, sampling, physics, the measured population, random error and personal odds.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从学科本身，延伸到汇总证据、显著性检验、抽样、物理学、被测量的总体、随机误差与个人风险概率。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many individual points are folded into a few summarizing bars.
core.cn: 核心意象：许多个别的数据点被折成少数几根概括性的柱子。

branches.en: THE DISCIPLINE: the whole toolkit of collecting, summarizing and testing data.
branches.cn: 学科整体：收集、汇总与检验数据的整套工具。

branches.en: THE MEASURED GROUP: evidence and the defined population from which it comes.
branches.cn: 被测量的群体：证据本身，以及证据所来自的被界定总体。

branches.en: CHANCE AND NOISE: results are judged against random scatter, and scatter is not blamed on the researcher.
branches.cn: 偶然与噪声：结果要对照随机离散来评判，而离散不应归咎于研究者。

branches.en: FROM SAMPLE TO CASE: conclusions about a whole, then odds applied back to one person.
branches.cn: 从样本到个案：先对整体下结论，再把概率反用于某个人。

branches.en: MANY-PARTICLE LIMIT: temperature and pressure exist only as averages over enormous numbers.
branches.cn: 多粒子极限：温度与压强只作为极大量粒子的平均值而存在。

intro.en: Statistical is statistics plus the adjective ending -al. The base statistics is a German academic coinage resting on New Latin statisticum, itself built on Latin status.
intro.cn: statistical 是 statistics 加形容词词尾 -al。词基 statistics 是德国学界的造词，建立在新拉丁 statisticum 之上，后者又由拉丁 status 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin line runs status 'state, condition' from stare 'to stand', then New Latin statisticum 'of state affairs', then German Statistik and English statistics.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁线索是 status「国家、状态」（出自 stare「站立」）→ 新拉丁 statisticum「与国家事务有关的」→ 德语 Statistik → 英语 statistics。

items.example: The journal requires a statistical review of every trial.
items.exampleCN: 该期刊要求对每项试验进行统计审查。

items.structure: German Statistik, from New Latin statisticum
items.meaning: the science of data, or a body of data
items.example: The statistics show a steady rise in enrolment.
items.exampleCN: 统计数据显示入学人数稳步上升。

items.example: The mean is the simplest statistic in the table.
items.exampleCN: 平均数是表中最简单的统计量。

items.example: A statistician checked the sampling plan.
items.exampleCN: 一位统计学家检查了抽样方案。

items.example: The two groups were statistically equivalent at the start.
items.exampleCN: 两组在开始时统计上相当。

items.example: Check the player's stats before the match.
items.exampleCN: 赛前先看看这名球员的数据。

items.example: Biostatistics guides the design of clinical trials.
items.exampleCN: 生物统计学指导临床试验的设计。

items.meaning: official figures on births, deaths and marriages
items.meaningCN: 关于出生、死亡与婚姻的官方数据
items.example: Vital statistics recorded a falling birth rate.
items.exampleCN: 生命统计记录了出生率下降。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 表示「属于……」的形容词词尾

definition_zh: 两个人依法律或习俗结成的夫妻关系，也指确立这种关系的婚礼
definition_en: the legally or socially recognized union of two people as spouses, and the ceremony that establishes it
core_image: 一张铺着红纸的桌上并排放着两只旧戒指、一份证书和一把新房钥匙
scene: 老屋的堂屋里点着两支红烛，墙上贴着一张写满吉利话的纸。 Her grandparents' marriage began with a ceremony that lasted three days.
sceneCN: 这里 marriage 指「两人依俗结成的夫妻结合」（第 1 个义项：由仪式与公认确立的配偶关系）；句意为她祖父母的婚姻始于一场持续三天的婚礼。可辨识物件：红烛、喜字、戒指、证书、钥匙；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 婚姻；结婚
婚礼

senses.title: The recognized union of spouses
senses.titleCN: 被法律或社会承认的夫妻结合
senses.definition: the state in which two people are legally or socially recognized as spouses
senses.definitionCN: 两个人被法律或社会承认为配偶的状态
senses.example: Their marriage was registered at the county office in spring.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的婚姻是春天在县里登记的。
senses.why: from Latin maritus 'husband', the noun names the wedded state itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词来自拉丁 maritus「丈夫」，直接指已婚状态本身。

senses.title: The wedding ceremony itself
senses.definition: the event in which vows are exchanged and the union is publicly made
senses.definitionCN: 交换誓言并公开确立结合的那场活动
senses.example: The whole village came to the marriage and stayed for the feast.
senses.exampleCN: 全村人都来参加婚礼，并留下来吃喜宴。
senses.why: the event and the state share one word because the rite is what creates the relation.
senses.whyCN: 仪式与状态共用一个词，因为正是仪式造成了这层关系。

senses.title: The ongoing state of being wed
senses.definition: the daily condition of living as a married couple over many years
senses.definitionCN: 多年来作为夫妻共同生活的日常状态
senses.example: Thirty years of marriage had taught them how to argue without wounding.
senses.exampleCN: 三十年的婚姻教会他们如何争吵却不伤人。
senses.why: the noun covers duration, not only the moment of union.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词涵盖持续时间，而不只是结合的那一刻。

senses.title: A type of marriage system
senses.definition: a socially defined form such as monogamy or polygyny, studied as a rule of the group
senses.definitionCN: 如一夫一妻或一夫多妻这类被社会定义的制度，作为群体规则来研究
senses.example: The community practiced marriage between cross-cousins.
senses.exampleCN: 这个社群实行交叉表亲之间的婚姻。
senses.why: societies classify forms of union, and the same noun labels the type.
senses.whyCN: 社会会给结合形式分类，同一个名词也就用来指类型。

senses.title: A close alliance between things
senses.titleCN: 事物之间的紧密结合（比喻义）
senses.definition: a metaphor for two different elements joined so closely that neither keeps its old shape
senses.definitionCN: 比喻两种不同成分紧密结合，彼此都不再保持原样
senses.example: The album is a marriage of folk melody and electronic rhythm.
senses.exampleCN: 这张专辑是民歌曲调与电子节奏的结合。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps the core idea of two parties becoming one.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留了「两方成为一体」的核心意思。

senses.title: A card game of matching pairs
senses.definition: a card game in which players collect matching pairs, named after the paired union
senses.definitionCN: 玩家收集同名对子的一种纸牌游戏，因配对而成名
senses.example: The old men played marriage beside the stove all evening.
senses.exampleCN: 老人们整晚在炉边玩配对纸牌。
senses.why: the game is named for the matched pair, echoing the union sense.
senses.whyCN: 这种游戏因成对的牌而得名，与「结合」义呼应。

senses.title: A religious sacrament
senses.definition: the union regarded as a sacred vow rather than only a civil contract
senses.definitionCN: 被视为神圣誓约、而非仅是民事契约的结合
senses.example: The church treats marriage as a vow made before God.
senses.exampleCN: 教会把婚姻视为在神面前立下的誓约。
senses.why: religions read the union as sacred, adding a layer the law does not supply.
senses.whyCN: 宗教把这种结合读作神圣的，添加了法律不提供的一层。

senses.title: A political alliance between families
senses.definition: a union arranged to bind two families, courts or states rather than two individuals
senses.definitionCN: 为联结两个家族、宫廷或国家而非两个个人而安排的婚姻
senses.example: The treaty was sealed by a marriage between the two courts.
senses.exampleCN: 条约由两个宫廷之间的联姻加以巩固。
senses.why: kinship was once a diplomatic instrument, and the noun named that instrument.
senses.whyCN: 亲属关系曾是外交工具，这个词就指那件工具。

senses.title: The legal registration of the union
senses.titleCN: 婚姻的法律登记与效力
senses.definition: the recorded act that gives the union standing in courts and in inheritance law
senses.definitionCN: 使这种结合在法院与继承法中生效的登记行为
senses.example: Without registration, the marriage had no standing in court.
senses.exampleCN: 没有登记，这段婚姻在法庭上不具效力。
senses.why: modern states turn the relation into a recorded fact with legal consequences.
senses.whyCN: 现代国家把这种关系变成一项带有法律后果的登记事实。

intro.en: Marriage reaches English through Old French mariage from Latin maritare 'to wed', a verb built on maritus 'husband'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: marriage 经古法语 mariage 来自拉丁 maritare「使成婚」，该动词由 maritus「丈夫」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Maritus meant 'husband, married man', with the feminine marita 'wife'. Its deeper origin is uncertain: the link to mas 'male' is often proposed but not demonstrated.
items.cn: maritus 意为「丈夫、已婚男子」，阴性形式为 marita「妻子」。其更深来源不确定：把它与 mas「男性」联系起来是常见假说，但未获证实。

items.en: Maritare meant 'to wed, to give in marriage', and was also used of joining a vine to a supporting tree, an image of two lives bound together.
items.cn: maritare 意为「使成婚、嫁娶」，也用于把葡萄藤接到支撑的树上，暗含两条生命被绑在一起。

items.en: Old French mariage named both the wedded state and the wedding feast, and carried both senses into English in the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 mariage 同时指已婚状态与婚宴，并在十三世纪把这两个义项带入英语。

items.en: English marriage kept the double sense from the start, so the same word names the relation and the day that begins it.
items.cn: 英语 marriage 从一开始就保留双重含义，同一个词既指关系，也指开启关系的那一天。

items.en: Canon law made marriage one of the sacraments, while civil law made it a contract with property consequences; both uses shaped the modern word.
items.cn: 教会法把婚姻列为圣事之一，世俗法则把它变成带有财产后果的契约；两种用法共同塑造了现代词义。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): no convincing Latin derivation of maritus has been established, and the recorded first uses of the card-game sense are not fixed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：maritus 尚无令人信服的拉丁派生来源；纸牌游戏义的最早书证年代也不固定。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same Latin stock; group two holds near synonyms for the union or the event.
note.cn: 第一组是同出这一拉丁词干的词；第二组是表示结合或仪式的近义词。

entries.definition: To take as a spouse or to join two people as spouses; marriage is the resulting state or event.
entries.definitionCN: 指娶、嫁或为两人证婚；marriage 是由此形成的状态或事件。

entries.definition: Of or relating to marriage, used in legal and medical contexts rather than in everyday talk.
entries.definitionCN: 指与婚姻有关的形容词，多用于法律与医学语境，而非日常口语。

entries.definition: A formal or religious word for the married state, felt as more solemn than marriage.
entries.definitionCN: 指已婚状态正式或宗教性的说法，比 marriage 更显庄重。

entries.definition: An old borrowing of the same French word, later displaced by marriage; it survives only in historical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 同一法语词的古老借形，后来被 marriage 取代，只在历史文献中留存。

entries.definition: The ceremony and its celebration, without saying anything about the years that follow.
entries.definitionCN: 只指仪式及其庆祝，不涉及婚后的岁月。

entries.definition: A general word for two things becoming one, used of states, trade bodies and couples alike.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指两物合而为一，国家、工会与伴侣都可使用。

entries.definition: A formal, often journalistic word for a wedding, always plural and slightly ornamental.
entries.definitionCN: 指婚礼的正式用语，常见于报道，总是复数且略带修饰色彩。

entries.definition: A lasting arrangement between two people or firms; it makes no claim about vows or law.
entries.definitionCN: 指两人或两家公司之间的长期安排，不涉及誓言或法律。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real word partnerships and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: maritus meant husband, and -age turns the person into the state: the husband-state, then the union.
normal.cn: maritus 指丈夫，-age 把人变成状态：先是「丈夫的身份」，再是婚姻。

normal.en: The family runs marry, marriage, marital, premarital, extramarital and marriageable.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 marry、marriage、marital、premarital、extramarital 与 marriageable。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: arranged marriage, marriage vows, marriage license, marriage of convenience.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：包办婚姻、结婚誓言、结婚证书、权宜婚姻。

normal.en: The metaphor is alive in phrases like a marriage of flavours or a marriage of styles.
normal.cn: 比喻义仍活跃，如风味的结合、风格的结合。

normal.en: The card game sense survives in regional play and in dictionaries, not in general speech.
normal.cn: 纸牌义仍留在地方玩法与词典中，日常口语已不常用。

abstract.en: Picture two streams meeting and then sharing one bed.
abstract.cn: 想象两条溪流汇合后共用一条河床。

abstract.en: Picture a knot tied in public and carried privately for years.
abstract.cn: 想象一个当众打好的结，被私人携带多年。

abstract.en: Picture a vine grafted onto a tree so that both keep growing.
abstract.cn: 想象一根藤接到树上，两者都继续生长。

examples.en: The law recognizes a marriage only after both parties sign the register.
examples.cn: 法律只有在双方签署登记簿后才承认婚姻。

examples.en: Their marriage survived drought, debt and two long separations.
examples.cn: 他们的婚姻熬过了干旱、债务与两次长期分离。

examples.en: Critics called the novel a marriage of detective plot and family saga.
examples.cn: 评论家称这部小说是侦探情节与家族史诗的结合。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「marry（结婚）+ age（年龄）」——到了年纪就结婚

root: 拉丁 maritus「丈夫」（阴性 marita「妻子」）→ 动词 maritare「使成婚」→ 古法语 mariage → 英语 marriage。maritus 的更深来源不确定，与 mas「男性」的联系仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one bond: two people are joined, and the joining is then read as an event, a daily state, a social rule, a metaphor, a game, a sacrament, a treaty and a register entry.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一个结合展开：两个人被连在一起，这个结合再依次被读作事件、日常状态、社会制度、比喻、游戏、圣事、盟约与登记记录。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two rings set side by side on one sheet of paper, neither complete without the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：两枚戒指并排放在同一张纸上，缺一枚都不成双。

branches.en: THE BOND AND ITS RECORD: the relation comes first, and the register is how a state sees it.
branches.cn: 结合与记录：关系在先，登记则是国家看见它的方式。

branches.en: THE DAY AND THE VOW: a public rite turns a private promise into a recognised union.
branches.cn: 那一天与那誓言：公开仪式把私下承诺变成被承认的结合。

branches.en: THE LONG MIDDLE: most of a marriage is neither the wedding nor the law but ordinary duration.
branches.cn: 漫长的中间段：婚姻的大部分既不是婚礼也不是法律，而是平常的持续。

branches.en: RULES AND ALLIANCES: a group can define the form, and families can use it as a treaty.
branches.cn: 规则与联盟：群体可以规定形式，家族也可以把它当作条约。

branches.en: TWO BECOME ONE: the metaphor and the card game both play on the matched pair.
branches.cn: 合二为一：比喻义与纸牌义都借成对之物做文章。

intro.en: Marriage is a Latin noun stem plus a French ending, and the same stem builds the legal, medical and everyday words around it.
intro.cn: marriage 由一个拉丁名词词干加一个法语词尾构成，同一词干还构成它周围的法律、医学与日常用词。

latinIntro.en: Latin maritus and marita sit behind marriage, marry and marital; the ending -age names a state or a collection.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 maritus 与 marita 是 marriage、marry 与 marital 的来源；词尾 -age 表状态或集合。

items.example: Maritus supplied the whole family of words.
items.exampleCN: maritus 提供了整个词族的来源。

items.example: The feminine form fills out the pair.
items.exampleCN: 阴性形式补全了这一对。

items.structure: maritare, maritavi, maritatum (Latin verb, first conjugation)
items.example: The verb could also mean to join a vine to a tree.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词也可指把藤接到树上。

items.example: The suffix turns the act of wedding into a lasting state.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把成婚之举变成持续状态。

items.example: Old French kept both senses in one word.
items.exampleCN: 古法语用一个词保留了这两个义项。

items.example: English kept the double sense intact.
items.exampleCN: 英语完整保留了这双重含义。

items.example: Marry is the verb behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: marry 是名词背后的动词。

items.meaning: relating to a husband or to marriage
items.example: Marital law speaks of duties between spouses.
items.exampleCN: 婚姻法讲的是配偶之间的义务。

items.example: Premarital agreements are signed before the wedding.
items.exampleCN: 婚前协议在婚礼之前签署。

items.example: Extramarital adds the idea of crossing a boundary.
items.exampleCN: extramarital 增添了越界的意思。

definition_zh: 工程师；设计并建造机器、结构或系统的人；也指巧妙地安排或促成
definition_en: a person who designs and builds machines, structures or systems; also to arrange or bring something about by skill
core_image: 一个戴着安全帽的人蹲在图纸与实物之间，用手比量一处接缝，然后在纸上改掉一个数字
scene: 工地上，戴安全帽的人蹲在图纸与钢梁之间，用手比量一处接缝，又在纸上改掉一个数字。 The engineer changed one dimension and the whole frame became cheaper to build.
sceneCN: 这里 engineer 指设计并建造结构的人（第 1 个义项：工程师这一职业的人）；句意：这位工程师改动了一个尺寸，整个框架的建造成本便降低了。

pos.zh: 工程师；设计师；轮机员
设计建造；巧妙地促成

senses.title: One who designs and builds
senses.definition: a person who applies technical knowledge to make machines, structures or systems work
senses.definitionCN: 运用技术知识使机器、结构或系统运转的人
senses.example: The engineer walked the site before agreeing to the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师先走了一遍现场，才同意那套方案。
senses.why: the -eer ending marks the agent, so the word begins as the person who works with engines.
senses.whyCN: 词尾标记施事者，因此这个词最初指与器械打交道的人。

senses.title: A licensed professional title
senses.definition: a formally qualified and often registered practitioner with legal responsibility for designs
senses.definitionCN: 具备正式资格、常需注册并对设计负法律责任的从业者
senses.example: Only a licensed engineer may sign the structural drawings.
senses.exampleCN: 只有持证工程师才能在结构图上签字。
senses.why: when public safety depends on a signature, the occupation becomes a protected title.
senses.whyCN: 当公共安全系于一个签名，这个职业就变成受保护的头衔。

senses.title: The one who runs an engine
senses.definition: the crew member responsible for a ship's or train's engines and machinery
senses.definitionCN: 船上或火车上负责发动机与机械的船员或乘务员
senses.example: The engine room answered to the engineer, not to the captain.
senses.exampleCN: 轮机舱听工程师的，而不是听船长的。
senses.why: the oldest everyday sense is the person in charge of the engine itself, a mechanic rather than a designer.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的日常义是掌管发动机本身的人，是技工而不是设计者。

senses.title: To design and construct
senses.definition: to plan and build something so that it meets a technical requirement
senses.definitionCN: 为使某物满足技术要求而规划并建造
senses.example: They engineered the tunnel to drain itself without pumps.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把隧道设计成无需水泵即可自排水。
senses.why: the noun's work becomes a verb the moment people speak of doing what the person does.
senses.whyCN: 当人们开始说「做这个人的事」，名词的工作就变成了动词。

senses.title: To arrange cleverly
senses.definition: to plan a situation so that a desired result follows
senses.definitionCN: 安排局面，使预期结果随之出现
senses.example: They engineered a delay that nobody could object to.
senses.exampleCN: 他们安排了一次谁也挑不出毛病的延迟。
senses.why: planned construction of a situation uses the same skill as planned construction of a bridge.
senses.whyCN: 安排局面与建造桥梁运用同一种「有计划的搭建」技能。

senses.title: To bring about by manipulation
senses.definition: to cause an outcome by quietly controlling the conditions
senses.definitionCN: 通过悄悄控制条件造成某个结果
senses.example: The result was engineered long before the vote.
senses.exampleCN: 那个结果早在投票之前就被促成了。
senses.why: the neutral verb darkens when the arrangement is hidden, because control without disclosure is manipulation.
senses.whyCN: 当安排被隐藏时，这个中性动词就变暗，因为不公开的控制就是操纵。

senses.title: A military builder of works
senses.definition: a soldier trained to build bridges, roads and fortifications
senses.definitionCN: 受训修筑桥梁、道路与工事的军人
senses.example: A military engineer surveyed the crossing before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 一名军事工程人员在黎明前勘察了渡口。
senses.why: the title was born in armies, where engines meant siege machines.
senses.whyCN: 这个头衔诞生于军队，那时「器械」指攻城机械。

senses.title: A software professional
senses.definition: a person who designs and maintains programs and systems
senses.definitionCN: 设计并维护程序与系统的人
senses.example: The engineer fixed the bug by removing a line, not adding one.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师删掉一行代码而不是加一行，就修好了那个缺陷。
senses.why: programs are now built things, so their builders inherit the old title without any metal involved.
senses.whyCN: 程序如今也是被建造之物，其建造者便继承了旧头衔，尽管不涉及金属。

senses.title: The on-site technical specialist
senses.definition: the person who installs, tests and repairs equipment where it is used
senses.definitionCN: 在使用现场安装、测试与维修设备的人
senses.example: A field engineer arrived with two replacement boards.
senses.exampleCN: 一位现场工程师带着两块备用板赶到。
senses.why: design and repair split into separate roles, and both keep the same broad title.
senses.whyCN: 设计与维修分成两种角色，两者都保留同一个宽泛头衔。

senses.title: One who alters living material
senses.definition: a specialist who redesigns genes or organisms
senses.definitionCN: 重新设计基因或生物体的专业人员
senses.example: The genetic engineer checked the sequence twice before proceeding.
senses.exampleCN: 基因工程师在继续之前把序列检查了两遍。
senses.why: the trade word follows its new materials, so a person who edits heredity is titled like a builder.
senses.whyCN: 行业词随新材料而延伸，编辑遗传的人也被冠以建造者式的头衔。

intro.en: Engineer is a person-word built on engine, from Latin ingenium, inborn talent. It began with military machines and widened to anyone who plans and builds.
intro.cn: engineer 是在 engine 之上构成的人物名词，而 engine 来自拉丁语 ingenium「天生才能」。它始于军用器械，后来扩大到一切规划与建造的人。

items.en: Latin ingenium meant natural talent and, by extension, a thing produced by talent, including a clever device.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ingenium 指天生的才能，引申指才能所造之物，包括巧妙的装置。

items.en: Old French engin meant both wit and a contrivance, and siege engines gave the word its military weight.
items.cn: 古法语 engin 兼指机智与装置，攻城器械给了这个词军事分量。

items.en: English engine covered any machine before steam narrowed it to a motor, a narrowing that came later than the person-word.
items.cn: 英语 engine 曾泛指任何机器，蒸汽时代才收窄为发动机，而这个收窄晚于人物名词的出现。

items.en: The engineer was first the soldier or craftsman who built and worked siege engines, then any builder of public works.
items.cn: engineer 最初指建造与操作攻城器械的士兵或工匠，后来指任何公共工程的建造者。

items.en: Roads, canals and railways turned military builders into civil professionals, and the title spread to every branch of construction.
items.cn: 道路、运河与铁路把军事建造者变成民用专业人员，这个头衔扩散到各个建造分支。

items.en: The twentieth century added software, genetic and financial uses, all sharing the sense of deliberate design.
items.cn: 二十世纪又添上软件、基因与金融用法，共同点是「有意的设计」。

note.en: The first group is the same root in its other roles; the second group is the neighbouring technical occupations.
note.cn: 第一组是同一词根的其他角色；第二组是相邻的技术职业。

entries.definition: The profession and activity; the engineer is the person inside it.
entries.definitionCN: 指职业与活动；engineer 是从事其中的人。

entries.definition: The motor or device itself; the person-word was formed from it, not the other way round.
entries.definitionCN: 指发动机或装置本身；人物名词由它构成，而不是反过来。

entries.definition: Deliberately designed, or brought about by arrangement, depending on the object.
entries.definitionCN: 指经有意设计，或指被安排促成，视宾语而定。

entries.definition: Belonging to the engineer, as in an engineer's drawing; it is not a separate word.
entries.definitionCN: 表示属于工程师，如「工程师的图纸」；它不是另一个词。

entries.definition: A person trained to run and maintain equipment; an engineer usually also designs it.
entries.definitionCN: 受训操作与维护设备的人；engineer 通常还要设计。

entries.definition: A person who repairs machines; the engineer may have designed what the mechanic fixes.
entries.definitionCN: 修理机器的人；engineer 可能正是设计了该机器的人。

entries.definition: A person who plans a form; the engineer's planning is constrained by physics and safety.
entries.definitionCN: 规划形态的人；engineer 的规划受物理与安全约束。

entries.definition: The designer of buildings; the engineer settles structure and services beneath that design.
entries.definitionCN: 建筑设计者；engineer 负责设计之下的结构与设备。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations from the real suffix and the real pair of noun and verb.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：来自真实词尾以及名词与动词的真实成对关系。

normal.en: The ending -eer marks a person, as in mountaineer and auctioneer.
normal.cn: 词尾 -eer 标记人物，如 mountaineer、auctioneer。

normal.en: The verb repeats the noun's forms: engineers, engineered, engineered, engineering.
normal.cn: 动词重复名词的形式：engineers、engineered、engineered、engineering。

normal.en: Two objects split the verb: engineer a bridge, engineer a delay.
normal.cn: 两类宾语分开动词：设计一座桥，促成一次延迟。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: civil engineer, chief engineer, field engineer.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：土木工程师、总工程师、现场工程师。

normal.en: The title began in armies and ended up in software, which shows how far a person-word can travel.
normal.cn: 这个头衔从军队开始，最后进了软件业，可见人物名词能走多远。

abstract.en: Picture a hand measuring a joint that exists only on paper, and the paper answering back.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在量只存在于纸上的接缝，而纸竟然回了话。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge that keeps a copy of its builder inside one of its bolts.
abstract.cn: 想象一座桥把建造者的影子留在一颗螺栓里。

abstract.en: Picture a schedule rearranged by someone who never touches the clock.
abstract.cn: 想象一张时间表被一个从不碰钟的人重新排列。

examples.en: The engineer refused to approve a joint she could not calculate.
examples.cn: 那位工程师拒绝批准一处她算不出来的接缝。

examples.en: They engineered the drainage so that the field would dry by itself.
examples.cn: 他们把排水设计得让田地能自行变干。

examples.en: A field engineer can fix in an hour what took a year to design.
examples.cn: 现场工程师能在一小时内修好设计花了一年才做出的东西。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「恩（en）机（gi）捏（neer）」——承恩于机器、亲手去捏的人，就是工程师

root: 拉丁 ingenium「天生才能」→ 古法语 engin「巧器」→ 英语 engine；加施事后缀构成 engineer，最初指造军用器械者，后泛指设计建造者，并转出动词用法。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses run from the designing professional through the licensed title, the engine operator, the two verb uses, military and software roles, field work and the editing of living material.
sensesIntro.cn: 十个义项从设计者出发，经过持证头衔、轮机操作者、两种动词用法、军事与软件角色、现场工作，最后到生物材料的改造者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a helmeted figure crouched between drawings and steel, measuring a joint and changing a number.
core.cn: 核心意象：戴安全帽的人蹲在图纸与钢梁之间，量一处接缝，改掉一个数字。

branches.en: BUILDERS OF THINGS: the general designer-builder, and the specialist who edits living material.
branches.cn: 建造者：泛指设计与建造的人，以及编辑生物材料的专家。

branches.en: TITLES AND ROLES: a licensed professional who signs drawings, a specialist on site, and the military builder of works.
branches.cn: 头衔与角色：在图纸上签字的持证者、现场作业的专员，以及军中修筑工事的人。

branches.en: ENGINE KEEPER: the mechanic in the engine room, the oldest everyday meaning.
branches.cn: 管机器的人：轮机舱里的技工，最古老的日常含义。

branches.en: BUILDING BY DESIGN: constructing to a requirement, and building programs rather than metal.
branches.cn: 按设计建造：按需求建造，以及建造程序而非金属。

branches.en: ARRANGING OUTCOMES: skilled arrangement in the open, and quiet manipulation behind it.
branches.cn: 安排结果：公开的巧妙安排，以及其背后的隐秘操纵。

intro.en: Engineer is engine with an agent ending; the same base then takes -ing for the field and -ed for the participle.
intro.cn: engineer 是 engine 加施事词尾；同一词基再加 -ing 成为领域名词，加 -ed 成为分词。

latinIntro.en: Latin ingenium is the deep base; French engin and the French agent ending -ier shaped the person-word before English took it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ingenium 是深远词基；法语 engin 与法语施事词尾 -ier 在英语借入前已塑成这个人物名词。

items.example: The noun already joins a person's gift to a made thing.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词已把人的天赋与造物连在一起。

items.example: French gave the base its military colour.
items.exampleCN: 法语给这个词基添上军事色彩。

items.example: The base names the thing the person works with.
items.exampleCN: 词基指这个人打交道的对象。

items.example: The ending is the same one seen in mountaineer.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾与 mountaineer 中所见相同。

items.example: The ending turns the person into a profession.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把人变成一门职业。

items.example: An engineered part has been through deliberate design.
items.exampleCN: 经工程设计的零件走过了有意的设计。

items.example: The ending marks what can be designed technically.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾标记可以被技术设计的东西。

items.example: Reverse engineering takes a product apart to learn it.
items.exampleCN: 逆向工程把产品拆开来学习。

definition_zh: 验证；确认……有效；使生效；批准认可
definition_en: to prove or confirm that something is valid, true or legally effective
core_image: 窗口前，一张表格递进来，工作人员在最后一栏盖上圆形印章，纸上的内容立刻有了效力
scene: 窗口前，一张表格递进来，工作人员在最后一栏盖上圆形印章，纸上的内容立刻有了效力。 Engineers validate every sensor against a known standard.
sceneCN: 这里指检验并确认某物符合标准（第 1 个义项：验证数据或器件有效）；句意为工程师用已知标准校验每一个传感器。

pos.zh: 验证；确认有效；使生效；批准

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加表示动作结果的名词尾构成，义为「验证；生效；认可」
由该动词加表示施动者的名词尾构成，义为「验证者；校验器」
由该动词的过去分词转成的形容词，义为「已验证的；已生效的」
由该动词的现在分词转成的形容词，义为「起验证作用的」

senses.title: Check data against a standard
senses.definition: to test measurements or records against a known rule to show that they are sound
senses.definitionCN: 用已知规则检验测量值或记录，以证明它们可靠
senses.example: The lab validates each batch of samples before release.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室在放行之前验证每一批样品。
senses.why: The root means strong, and the verb asks whether a result can stand up to a standard.
senses.whyCN: 词根意为「强、有力」，而这个动词问的是：一项结果能否在标准面前站得住。

senses.title: Confirm a claim or hypothesis
senses.definition: to give evidence that a statement or theory is correct
senses.definitionCN: 提供证据说明某项陈述或理论是正确的
senses.example: New evidence validated his earlier claim.
senses.exampleCN: 新证据证实了他先前的说法。
senses.why: A claim is valid when it holds, and the verb names the act of showing that it holds.
senses.whyCN: 主张站得住就叫有效，而这个动词命名的正是证明它站得住的动作。

senses.title: Give legal force to a document
senses.definition: of a court or official, to declare a will, contract or act legally effective
senses.definitionCN: 指法院或官员宣布遗嘱、合同或行为在法律上有效
senses.example: The judge validated the will after the hearing.
senses.exampleCN: 听证之后，法官确认了遗嘱的效力。
senses.why: This is the sense where the word does not merely check but confers force; validation changes the legal status.
senses.whyCN: 在这个义项里，词不只是检查，而是授予效力；「确认有效」改变了法律地位。

senses.title: Approve a plan or decision
senses.definition: of a body with authority, to accept a proposal and allow it to proceed
senses.definitionCN: 指有权的机构接受提案并允许其推进
senses.example: The board validated the plan at its monthly meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会在月度会议上批准了该计划。
senses.why: Approval is a stamp that makes a paper count, which is the image the word carries in administration.
senses.whyCN: 批准是一枚让纸张算数的印章，这正是这个词在行政语境里携带的意象。

senses.title: Prove a ticket or identity
senses.definition: to check that a ticket, pass or document belongs to the person using it
senses.definitionCN: 检查票证或文件是否属于使用它的人
senses.example: The gate validates each ticket before the concert.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐会在入场前逐一验票。
senses.why: A ticket is valid only for one holder and one time, and the verb is the act of confirming both.
senses.whyCN: 一张票只对一位持有者和一个时间有效，而这个动词就是确认这两件事的动作。

senses.title: Check that input is acceptable
senses.definition: in computing, to test data entered by a user against the rules a system requires
senses.definitionCN: 计算机中指按系统规则检验用户输入的数据
senses.example: The app validates the form before sending it.
senses.exampleCN: 应用在发送之前会校验表单。
senses.why: Software borrowed the word because a form either meets the rule or does not, exactly like a document before a clerk.
senses.whyCN: 软件借用这个词，因为表单要么符合规则、要么不符合，正如文件到了办事员面前。

senses.title: Test a model or method
senses.definition: to show that a model, instrument or procedure produces trustworthy results
senses.definitionCN: 证明模型、仪器或程序能产生可信结果
senses.example: The team validated the model with a second data set.
senses.exampleCN: 团队用第二套数据验证了该模型。
senses.why: A model is valid when it works beyond the cases that built it, and validation is the test of that reach.
senses.whyCN: 模型能在建造它的案例之外也起作用才算有效，而验证就是对这份覆盖力的测试。

senses.title: Recognize someone's feelings
senses.definition: in psychology, to affirm that another person's emotional experience is real and understandable
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中指确认他人的情感体验是真实、可理解的
senses.example: A good listener validates what the speaker feels.
senses.exampleCN: 好的倾听者会认可说话者的感受。
senses.why: Here validity is granted to an inner state rather than to a document, and the word turns warm.
senses.whyCN: 这里被授予效力的是内心状态而不是文件，这个词也随之变暖。

senses.title: Confirm the standing of a qualification
senses.titleCN: 确认学历或资格的效力
senses.definition: of an authority, to accept a degree, licence or certificate as officially usable
senses.definitionCN: 指权威机构承认学位、执照或证书可正式使用
senses.example: The registry validates foreign qualifications case by case.
senses.exampleCN: 登记机构逐一确认海外学历的效力。
senses.why: A qualification is only useful where it is recognized, and the verb marks the boundary between holding and being able to use.
senses.whyCN: 资格只有在被承认的地方才有用，而这个动词标出「持有」与「能够使用」之间的界线。

intro.en: Validate comes from Medieval Latin validare, to make valid, from validus, strong, from valere, to be strong or be worth.
intro.cn: 这个词来自中世纪拉丁语 validare「使有效」，而 validare 出自 validus「强壮的」，其底层是 valere「有力、有价值」。

items.en: Valere meant to be strong, to be worth or to have influence, and it also gave English value and valour.
items.cn: valere 意为有力、有价值或有影响，它还给英语带来「价值」与「英勇」等词。

items.en: The adjective meant strong, sturdy or effective, and it became the everyday word for a sound argument or a sound body.
items.cn: 这个形容词意为强壮的、坚实的、有效的，后来成为形容论证可靠或身体强健的日常词。

items.en: Legal Latin formed a verb meaning to make valid or to give force to a document.
items.cn: 法律拉丁语造出一个动词，意为使有效、授予文件效力。

items.en: French carried the legal verb into administrative use before English borrowed it.
items.cn: 法语把这个法律动词带进行政用途，之后英语才借入。

items.en: English took the verb in the seventeenth century; the exact first date is uncertain, and the legal sense came first.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪取用这个动词；确切首见年代不确定，法律义最先出现。

items.en: Science and computing made it the standard verb for testing data, models and input against a rule.
items.cn: 科学与计算机使它成为按规则检验数据、模型与输入的标准动词。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like validate; the second group names neighbouring ways of confirming something.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与 validate 相近；第二组是与「确认、证实」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The act of proving something valid or giving it force.
entries.definitionCN: 指证明某物有效或授予其效力的行为。

entries.definition: A person or program that checks validity.
entries.definitionCN: 指检查有效性的个人或程序。

entries.definition: Sound, legally effective or based on good reasoning.
entries.definitionCN: 指可靠的、法律上有效的，或基于良好推理的。

entries.definition: The quality of being sound or legally effective.
entries.definitionCN: 指可靠或法律上有效的性质。

entries.definition: To make something void; it is built on the negative of the adjective, not on this verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指使某物失效；它建立在形容词的否定形式之上，而不是本动词之上。

entries.definition: To check whether a fact or figure is true; it asks about accuracy rather than effect.
entries.definitionCN: 指检查事实或数字是否真实；它追问准确与否，而非效力。

entries.definition: To show that something already believed is true; it adds certainty rather than force.
entries.definitionCN: 指表明原本已被相信的事是真的；增加的是确定性，而非效力。

entries.definition: To state officially, often in writing, that something meets a standard.
entries.definitionCN: 指以官方方式、常以书面形式声明某物符合标准。

entries.definition: To give formal approval to a treaty or agreement, making it binding.
entries.definitionCN: 指对条约或协议给予正式批准，使其具有约束力。

entries.definition: To support a claim with evidence; it stresses the proof offered.
entries.definitionCN: 指用证据支撑主张；强调所提供的证明。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the strong root, the stamp image and the contrast with mere checking.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想利用「有力」的词根、盖章的意象，以及它与单纯检查的对比。

normal.en: The root means strong, so something valid can stand; to validate is to show that it stands.
normal.cn: 词根意为有力，所以有效的东西站得住；而「验证」就是证明它站得住。

normal.en: A round stamp on the last column is the picture: the paper does not change, its force does.
normal.cn: 最后一栏上的圆形印章就是那幅图：纸没有变，变的是它的效力。

normal.en: A ticket is validated at the gate, a model at a second data set, a feeling by a good listener.
normal.cn: 票在闸口被验证，模型在第二套数据上被验证，感受由好的倾听者来确认。

normal.en: Verify asks whether it is true; validate asks whether it counts.
normal.cn: 「核实」问的是真假，「确认有效」问的是算不算数。

normal.en: The word can be cold in a laboratory and warm in a therapist's room, because validity applies to numbers and to feelings alike.
normal.cn: 这个词在实验室里是冷的，在治疗室里是暖的，因为「有效」既能用于数字，也能用于感受。

abstract.en: Validation is the moment a private fact becomes a public one.
abstract.cn: 验证，是一个私下的事实变成公开事实的那一刻。

abstract.en: To validate is to answer the question of whether something may be relied on.
abstract.cn: 验证就是回答「某物是否可以被依靠」这个问题。

abstract.en: The word grants standing, and standing is a social gift as much as a technical result.
abstract.cn: 这个词授予的是「站得住」的地位，而地位既是技术结果，也是社会赠予。

examples.en: The survey was validated by a second team.
examples.cn: 这项调查由第二个团队作了验证。

examples.en: The court validated the agreement in March.
examples.cn: 法院在三月确认了该协议的效力。

examples.en: Please validate your parking ticket at the desk.
examples.cn: 请在服务台确认停车票。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「瓦利得特」——「瓦」片盖印，「利」上生效，「得」到批准才「特」别算数：验证、使生效

root: 拉丁语 valere「有力、有价值」→ validus「强壮的、有效的」→ 中世纪拉丁语 validare「使有效」→ 法语 valider → 英语 validate「验证；使生效；批准」；核心是「让某物在标准或权威面前站得住」。
